papers.title: Post-processing strategies for generative design outcomes in a UAV tail boom
papers.abstract: Abstract Generative design produces structurally efficient but organically shaped geometries that require post-processing before Fused Deposition Modeling (FDM) manufacturing. This paper compares two post-processing strategies applied to the same generative design outcome for an Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) tail boom: a complex variant faithful to the raw topology, and a simplified variant with symmetric arms, self-supporting geometry, and uniform cross-sections oriented toward FDM manufacturability. Both variants were evaluated using linear static and buckling finite element analysis underidentical loading conditions. Scaled prototypes of the simplified variant were FDM-printed at two infill configurations and physically load-tested. The manufacturing-oriented simplification reduced both mass and print time while eliminating support structures; peak stress remained well below the material limit. FEA-predicted stress concentrations correlated with observed fracture locations in physical tests. For lightly loaded polymer FDM structures, these results suggest that manufacturing-oriented simplification of generative design outcomes incurs a negligible structural penalty while improving printability and reducing production cost.

papers.title: Safe and Interpretable Vehicle Platoon Control via Physics-Enhanced Residual Learning
papers.abstract: Abstract Vehicle platoon control in complex dynamic environments necessitates a rigorous balance between physical interpretability safety constraints and nonlinear compensation. This paper presents PERL, a Physics-Enhanced Residual Learning framework that hierarchically integrates Distributed Model Predictive Control (DMPC) with Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3) algorithm. To address the pathological residual action saturation. we propose a residual-magnitude-based action regularization mechanism. This mechanism penalizes large-amplitude residuals to stabilize the policy update and constrain the RL module within a safe, small-amplitude regime, ensuring effective compensation for unmodeled dynamics beyond the physical baseline’s fidelity. Additionally, a spatiotemporal smooth handover and dynamic fusion strategy significantly enhances edge-case safety. Utilizing safety-boundary constraints and dual soft-filtering, the strategy regulates control authority to mitigate violations of Rational Driving Constraints by RL policies while preventing abrupt control mutations. Experiments across four representative scenarios show that PERL converges rapidly and consistently outperforms MPC, PPO, and TD3 in safety, comfort, and platoon stability. Specifically, PERL reduces inverse time-to-collision by 20.3% relative to PPO and improves ride comfort by over 60% compared with TD3. Ultimately, the framework attains the lowest cumulative damping ratio, demonstrating superior string stability and robust generalization capability in real dynamic traffic environments.

papers.title: Remote nanomagnetic activation of mechanotransduction: principles, therapeutic applications, and translational challenges.
papers.abstract: Mechanical signaling is increasingly recognized as a therapeutic target and a key element of the stem cell niche in regenerative medicine and disease. Magnetic nanoparticles (MNPs) offer a practical route for delivering such cues because they can be actuated remotely, functionalized with ligands and incorporated into cells, scaffolds, hydrogels or assay platforms. Magnetically driven mechanotransduction provides evidence that MNPs can act not only as carriers, labels or heating agents, but as active interfaces controlling cell signaling and fate.This review places magnetic ion channel activation (MICA) within magnetic nanomedicine, including magnetic resonance imaging, targeted drug delivery, hyperthermia and magnetic biomaterials. Magneto-mechanical stimulation adds design variables including force, torque, surface functionalisation, target access and particle behavior at the biointerface. Particular attention is given to mechanosensitive targets, including TREK1, TRPV4, PIEZO1, integrins and Frizzled/Wnt signaling. Applications are graded by preclinical maturity: bone repair is best developed, followed by peripheral nerve, cartilage, immune and biofabrication work. A central theme is the evidence pipeline connecting acute cell-level signaling with tissue-level outcomes. Translational barriers include particle quality control, aggregation and protein-corona effects, internalization, field dosimetry, degradation, specificity and uneven reporting. A healthcare future will depend on standardized benchmark models, biogenic MNPs and long-term in vivo outcome data.

papers.title: Plan4D: Generative Plannable 4D Worlds
papers.abstract: Most world models for future prediction prioritize aestetic quality of generated videos, but offer only weak physical grounding and limited geometric consistency over time, due to the lack of explicit 4D modeling. In this paper, we introduce plan4d, a possible next milestone towards building a generative plannable 4D world model that predicts future RGB videos together with dense 4D geometry, including depth, cameras, point clouds, and scene flow from an observed scene context and text-specified actions. Since training data with paired actions and dense 4D annotations is inherently scarce, plan4d leverages the complementary priors of foundational video generators and 3D reconstructors. Specifically, we propose a model-stitching architecture that couples Depth Anything 3 with LongCat-Video and augments it with an auxiliary DPT head for scene-flow prediction. The resulting model allows us to plan and generate complex, long-horizon, and fine-grained actions in a dynamic 3D scenes, while substantially improving both visual fidelity and geometric accuracy of the generated future videos. Extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate that plan4d achieves state-of-the-art performance in generative 4D modeling of environmental reactions. papers.title: JARVIS: An Agent That Designs, Builds, and Tests Circuit Boards on Its Own
papers.abstract: Power electronics is central to the energy transition, but developing new hardware still relies on human-led design, fabrication, testing, and iteration. We present JARVIS, an embodied AI agent that autonomously closes this loop for circuit boards. JARVIS maintains machine-specific capabilities and constraints, scans its workspace using a robot-mounted 3D scanner, and constructs an executable digital twin in which it rehearses robot motions, fabrication steps, and circuit behavior before consuming materials. A single text instruction initiates the physical experiment. Using unmodified desktop equipment, the agent coordinates a robot arm, a PCB printer that deposits conductive silver ink and solder paste, and a pick-and-place machine. It verifies progress using cameras and sensors, then tests the fabricated circuit with an OPAL-RT real-time simulator and an oscilloscope. Based on the measurements, JARVIS diagnoses deviations from the design and generates a revised design in KiCad for subsequent rehearsal. In a demonstration involving a 60 Hz notch filter for grid-connected converter sensing, JARVIS completed a first-run experiment in 2 h 39 min without human intervention, achieving 50.6 dB attenuation at 60 Hz. Its digital-twin rehearsal identified five issues before fabrication, including a test criterion that would have incorrectly rejected a functioning board. During execution, the agent also resolved encountered faults autonomously. These results demonstrate an integrated agent-driven workflow for physical design, fabrication, measurement, and iterative improvement of power-electronic circuitry. To our knowledge, JARVIS is the first system in power electronics in which an agent closes the physical design-build-test-learn loop for circuit boards.

papers.title: Monte Carlo Pass Search for Setpieces
papers.abstract: Set pieces produce about a third of non-penalty expected goals (xG), yet they are usually evaluated by what happened next. We present Monte Carlo Pass Search (MCPS) for set pieces, which treats a corner or a lofted free kick as a distribution over plausible executions and plausible futures instead of a single realised event. From the pre-kick state, MCPS proposes counterfactual deliveries and counterfactual set-ups (where the attackers stand at the kick), plays each out many times in a world model (3D ball physics, a generative model of all 22 players, the keeper's come-or-stay decision and a Player-to-Touch model) and scores every future with a value model. On 249 deliveries from 30 Serie A 2025/26 matches, with every model applied only to matches it never saw, the best available delivery is worth 0.0085 xG more than the one kicked (+28 %), mainly because it reaches an attacker before the keeper. Searching where the attackers stand as well adds +0.0027 xG with the observed ball and +0.0033 on top of the best ball; designing their runs too adds +0.0007 more. We show how to keep such a search honest, and estimate how much more data each component needs before a club could rely on it.

papers.title: Neural Conditional Gaussian Model: Efficient Data Assimilation with Sequential Uncertainty Quantification for Nonlinear Dynamics
papers.abstract: Data assimilation (DA) in partially observed nonlinear systems requires repeated estimation of both hidden states and their uncertainty. Conventional nonlinear filtering can be computationally expensive and often relies on an explicit dynamical model. In this paper, we develop the Neural Conditional Gaussian Model (Neural CGM), a data-driven dynamical model that maps unobserved physical states into a learned latent space, where the dynamics of the latent states follow a conditional Gaussian structure. This structure allows closed-form DA updates in the latent space, while nonlinear encoder-decoder mappings retain the flexibility needed to represent complex dynamics in physical space. A key feature of Neural CGM is its treatment of uncertainty in DA. The latent posterior mean and covariance are mapped to the physical variables through a Gaussian decoder that combines local moment propagation with learned nonlinear corrections. The resulting physical-space posterior statistics depend on the sequentially updated latent distribution rather than on a separate post-processing estimate. The same statistics enter a Gaussian negative log-likelihood during training, so both the posterior mean and uncertainty affect the learned model. Because Neural CGM learns the dynamical model itself, it can also be used for state forecasting and simulation without explicit knowledge of the governing equations. Numerical experiments on benchmark nonlinear dynamical systems show accurate state estimation and forecasting while substantially reducing online assimilation cost relative to conventional nonlinear DA methods. Neural CGM is therefore suited to repeated state estimation, uncertainty quantification, and prediction from partial observations.

papers.title: Bayesian optimization on amortized search space
papers.abstract: In real-world black-box optimization problems, a mechanistic simulator is often available that approximately predicts the behavior of the system as a function of the parameters being optimized. Here, we show how an amortized inverse map of such a simulator can be used in Bayesian optimization to restrict the search space while using a Gaussian process kernel that is aware of the original problem geometry. This allows for efficiently leveraging the low intrinsic dimensionality of the optimization problem. We characterize its approximation bias and information gain, and derive an intrinsic-dimension-dependent regret rate under additional geometric and Gaussian Process assumptions. We illustrate the method with an application to drug dosing personalization in Parkinson's disease. We use, as a simulator, a pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) model of a drug, a mechanistic model calibrated on population data with quantified parameter uncertainty. A dosing neural network is trained offline against the model, amortizing the map from patient PK/PD parameters to the regimen predicted to be optimal, and online Bayesian optimization then searches over this learned, low-dimensional representation rather than over raw dosages. Numerical simulations demonstrate the improved performance of our method in this application, as well as under simulator misspecification.

papers.title: Should Belgians Install an Advanced Energy Management System in Their Electrified Dwelling ?
papers.abstract: As dwellings electrify and more complex electricity pricing spreads in Belgium, the question arises: What are the potential benefits of installing an advanced energy management systems in an electrified Belgian dwelling ?   To answer this question, we simulate 500 representative Belgian dwellings in which fossil systems are replaced by controllable electric technologies: space heating via air-to-air heat pumps, domestic hot water via electric boilers, and private transport via electric vehicles with home chargers. Photovoltaic systems are assigned according to current adoption rates.   We evaluate two advanced energy management systems (EMS): model predictive control (MPC) and TreeC, a machine learning method using decision trees to model the EMS strategy. These are compared to a rule-based controller (RBC) that mimics default operation and an MPC with perfect forecasts (MPC P) as an upper bound. Performance for these EMSs is assessed for 2023 under a real contract with hourly prices and a monthly peak tariff.   Average annual savings versus RBC are 82.5 EUR, 116.6 EUR, and 177.4 EUR for TreeC, MPC, and MPC P, respectively. All EMSs deliver similar thermal comfort (26-31 Kh). MPC saves more, while TreeC achieves higher EV charge completion (93.3% vs 88.8% for MPC, with a max charge of 95%) and a smoother aggregate load across the 500 dwellings. Savings remain modest relative to EMS purchase (280-680 EUR) and subscription (0-360 EUR/year) costs which is not favourable towards widespread adoption.   The data and code to reproduce this study are available at https://github.com/EVERGi/should_belgians_install_advanced_ems_paper.

papers.title: FEA solver integration of a composite World Model with a Spiking Neural Network memory Block for computationally efficient modelling of defects and variabilities
papers.abstract: Each fibre-reinforced composite structure has a unique material architecture. The manufacturing methods used and the presence of defects lead to local variations which require material-scale models that can resolve the response in real time at every location in the structure. Concurrent multi-scale schemes provide this capability, but at a prohibitive computational cost for large structures as the number of integration points and time increments scales with size. Surrogates have been studied extensively as replacements for material-scale models to mitigate these computational limitations. A surrogate must represent an arbitrary local architecture including defects, track the irreversible material state over an unknown number of increments, remain stable when driven recursively by its own predictions, and fit within the memory available at every integration point. Here, a Composites World Model based on a Multi-Modal Spiking Transformer architecture is designed to meet these requirements. The proposed architecture combines a material encoder, a Spiking Neural Network memory block that tracks the long-term internal state of the material, and transformer blocks that learn the short-term applied strain state. The system is trained in three stages: material architecture encoding, base training on short time windows, and recursive fine-tuning with scheduled sampling to suppress cumulative error drift. The trained model is disassembled at inference and coupled to a non-linear FE solver, enabling structural scale simulation of composites containing embedded defects. Benchmarks against experimental results for IM7/8552 laminates under tension, compression and transverse shear, for pristine and wrinkled composites, show that the SNN memory block successfully tracks the material internal state and results in prediction errors between 0.4% and 4.8%.

papers.title: How to Effectively Manage the Energy in Residential Systems: Development and Comparison of Methods

The thesis presents three simulation cases alongside one real-world experiment to compare energy management done through simple rules, optimization, and machine learning methods. Furthermore, this thesis introduces TreeC, a novel machine learning-based method that learns understandable yet efficient energy management strategies, applicable to many cases.   The three key contributions of this thesis can be summarized as follows: 1) The developed TreeC method demonstrates competitive performance compared to a variety of energy management approaches, such as model predictive control and reinforcement learning, across a diverse set of energy management problems. The understandability of TreeC's energy management strategies greatly improves the transparency and trustworthiness of machine learning-based energy management. 2) The real-world experiment highlights the need to validate energy management methods on actual hardware and not solely on simulations. Both TreeC and model predictive control performed worse than in simulations, due to, respectively, insufficiently representative training data and the real-time input data not being reliable enough. 3) Energy management algorithms reduce costs in electrified Belgian dwellings, particularly in poorly insulated dwellings, electric vehicle chargers, and photovoltaic installations. Displacement labels from ANSYS Additive Print simulations are mapped onto STL vertices using Gaussian-kernel weighted averaging. Evaluated on 117 parts using five-fold cross-validation split by part, the model achieves an R^2 of 0.946 and a mean absolute error of 0.0178 mm for displacement magnitude. GAT also outperforms GraphSAGE (R^2 = 0.936) and a graph convolutional network (R^2 = 0.934) across all five folds. Ablation experiments show that removing mass-distribution descriptors reduces magnitude R^2 to 0.900, while removing build-plate contact and overhang descriptors reduces it to 0.920. papers.title: Actor-Predictor Architecture for Reinforcement Learning with Formal Specification Objectives
papers.abstract: One fundamental challenge in reinforcement learning (RL) is enforcing temporal safety constraints, such as satisfying formal specifications. However, this approach assumes that automaton construction is both feasible and tractable, which limits its applicability to small specifications and linear temporal logic (LTL). This paper proposes Actor-Predictor, a framework that learns a surrogate representation of logic progress without explicitly constructing an automaton. The predictor continuously estimates whether a partial trajectory will satisfy the formal specification in a later step, and its learned features are provided as auxiliary inputs to the actor, which is then optimized using GRPO and RWR. We show theoretically that, under sufficient predictive accuracy, the learned representation is equivalent to the automaton state. Experiments on grid world and robotic tasks in Isaac Lab demonstrate that Actor-Predictor outperforms automaton-based baselines on LTL-constrained tasks. It also performs well on non-regular formal specifications, such as $(a^n b^n)$, for which finite-automaton-based approaches are not applicable.

papers.title: Physics-Informed Feature Representations and Pretrained Tabular Foundation Models for Generalizable Melt Pool Geometry Prediction

Conventional ML models typically use dimensional process parameters, which represent laser-material interactions only implicitly and may limit cross-material transfer. This study evaluates whether two physics-informed dimensionless features, normalized enthalpy and Peclet number, combining laser processing conditions with material thermophysical properties, improve melt pool prediction over raw process parameters. We systematically benchmark seven models: four classical ML methods (Gaussian process, support vector machine, random forest, and XGBoost) and three pretrained tabular foundation models (TabPFN, TabDPT, and TabICLv2). Experiments span 316L stainless steel, IN625, IN718, and combined-material datasets, covering regression of melt pool width and depth and classification of melting modes. Dimensionless features yield comparable or superior predictive performance in most settings, with the largest gains in cross-material depth prediction (R^2 = 0.96). Tabular foundation models generally achieve stronger classification performance than classical baselines, particularly for multi-material datasets. These findings indicate that combining physically meaningful dimensionless representations with pretrained tabular models can improve data-efficient melt pool modeling and support more transferable process-window identification in LPBF.

papers.abstract: Recently, video world models have advanced interactive generation, with large models offering higher quality and smaller models enabling faster inference. Existing speculative methods combine their strengths through fast draft generation and selective target regeneration guided by rewards on decoded frames. However, verification covers only the external scorer's evaluation dimensions and adds decoding and scoring costs. Moreover, these scores provide no correction, requiring costly target regeneration for rejected drafts. To address these limitations, we propose Speculative World Model (SpecWM), a unified, training-free inference framework for streaming world models. It verifies draft chunks using the target's latent velocity field. Verification also yields a reusable correction; two thresholds select Accept, Refine, or Reject. Specifically, one-step refinement reuses it to improve perceptual quality, while three-step refinement strengthens camera following and trajectory consistency. These findings motivate transition-aware refinement. On WBench Navigation, SpecWM improves visual quality at 1.63$\times$ speedup over the target and raises NavScore from the draft's 75.99 to 85.63, achieving the best quality-speed-control trade-off. Additionally, our LongSpecBench shows sustained quality and control over long, multi-turn rollouts, while experiments on Hy-Nomas validate SpecWM across backbones and denoising budgets.

papers.abstract: Stereo-electroencephalography (SEEG) represents the most effective technique for the detection of the Epileptogenic Zone (EZ) in drug-resistant epilepsy. Accordingly, we develop a detection algorithm that identifies the channels belonging to the EZ by quantifying, through the Kullback-Leibler divergence, the difference between their transition probabilities in the inter-ictal period and at seizure onset. We evaluate our framework in SEEG recordings from 30 patients with drug-resistant epilepsy and compare it with a benchmark that operates in the same observation space but does not consider a latent-state structure. Compared against medically validated EZ definitions, our study shows that modeling channel-specific temporal transitions can improve EZ localization and offer a data-driven framework to investigate the latent dynamics underlying seizures.

papers.title: Information-Region MPC: Non-Iterative Distributed Control of Urban Traffic Signals
papers.abstract: Centralized model predictive control (MPC) exploits network-wide traffic information to obtain the optimal solution of the network-level control problem, but its computational burden grows rapidly with network size. To address these limitations, this paper proposes information-region MPC (IR-MPC), which approximates the first control input of centralized MPC using limited real-time data without iterative coordination. Based on historical traffic data, we quantify how perturbations at other intersections affect the centralized first control input of each intersection and use these couplings to construct a compact information region for every intersection. At each control update, each intersection then solves a local IR-MPC problem once using current data only from its information region. SUMO simulations on a real 28-intersection network show that IR-MPC with one processor per intersection computes its control inputs 9 times faster than centralized MPC and 15 times faster than a representative iterative decomposition-based distributed MPC method. IR-MPC reproduces 85% of the centralized control inputs exactly at the implemented one-second resolution, keeps 99.3% within 2s, and increases mean delay by only 0.03%.

Such a guarantee, however, assumes that calibration and test data follow the same distribution, an assumption that is violated in orbital perception, where labelled calibration images are available only from synthetic renderings while operational images are real. In this work, we show on the SPEED+ dataset that conformal pose estimation calibrated on synthetic images loses its coverage guarantee on real images, and that many of the resulting failures are silent: the predicted pose set appears valid but excludes the true pose. To address this, we calibrate on synthetic images translated to the appearance of real images. Since translation alters appearance while preserving geometry, the synthetic pose labels remain valid and no labelled real images are required. Experiments with two translation models show that this calibration restores coverage above the specified level for miscoverage levels of 0.1 and above, and reduces silent failures from up to 43.5% to at most 3.3% of the test images, bringing conformal pose estimation a step closer to trustworthy deployment in space.

Specifically, we inject temporally correlated noise into the actions of a policy trained on task-agnostic human teleoperation. We then train the world model so that its generated videos respond to this noise as the recorded videos do, without requiring repeated executions from the same initial state. papers.title: Sample-efficient end-to-end Optical Music Recognition through Active Learning
papers.abstract: End-to-end approaches to Optical Music Recognition (OMR) have recently shown promising results, but their performance often degrades on unseen data. However, this process typically requires extensive manual annotation to yield competitive models, making it costly and time-consuming. In this work, we explore Active Learning to reduce this burden by selecting informative samples for labeling in low-resource scenarios, where the amount of manual annotation that can be performed is limited. Changing the sampling schedule reveals further differences official scores miss. In controlled physical systems with known outcome probabilities, our metric favors the true distribution over collapsed predictions. In short, a world model should be judged not only by how closely one video matches what happened, but by how faithfully its predictions represent what could have happened.

Pooled pass rates varied by under five percentage points across description authors. papers.title: Faithful Generative Modeling for Censored Time-to-Event Data: From Distributional Fidelity to Statistical Inference
papers.abstract: Synthetic data has emerged as a powerful tool for data sharing, clinical trial simulation, and digital twin development, with growing applications in biomedical research and drug development. However, limited attention has been devoted to synthetic time-to-event data, which are central to clinical trials and survival analysis. In particular, theoretical guarantees for the distributional fidelity of synthetic survival data remain largely unexplored. More importantly, even when a generator achieves distributional fidelity, it remains unclear whether the downstream statistical analysis is reliable. To address these gaps, we propose a general two-stage generative framework for survival data (TSGSurv) that jointly generates observed times and covariates conditional on event status, and establish its distributional convergence rate. Focusing on the widely used Cox proportional hazards model, we establish conditions under which generator fidelity guarantees consistency of model coefficient estimates. We further characterize the limitations of naive inference based on synthetic data, and develop a variance correction and a distribution calibration procedure to recover valid inference of original data. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed generative and inferential framework with extensive simulations and two real data applications.

papers.title: Stuck in Place: Stall Diagnosis and Remedies for JEPA Planners
papers.abstract: Joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA) world models plan from pixels with model predictive control, yet often fail on tasks their model should handle. Test-time adaptation attributes such failures to model error under distribution shift and updates the weights on the current episode, without checking this attribution against the planning loop itself. We follow the executed planning loop on pushing tasks. In most settings, with and without distribution shift, nearly all failures (at least 96%) are stalls, where the object stays in place while the model predicts progress. The warm-started gradient-descent (GD) planner then returns nearly the same plan, a fixed point where the agent mostly idles. We propose Unstick, which pairs on-policy fine-tuning before deployment with a fixed-weight loop breaker: a residual memory of the episode's prediction errors or random re-initialization at every replan. With GD, Unstick recovers most of the adaptation gain on pushing tasks with the memory, and with re-initialization most of it on shape shifts but much less on visual shifts. A large part of what limits these planners under GD is thus a fixed point of the planning loop, present with and without distribution shift, which a planner with fixed weights can break. Code is available at https://github.com/jhlee0619/unstick.

papers.title: Differentiable Hydrodynamics for Whole-Body MPC of Underwater Robots
papers.abstract: Underwater vehicle-manipulator systems distribute actuation across thrusters and joint motors. Whole-body model predictive control (MPC), rather than separate vehicle and arm controllers, can coordinate both to extend the workspace and exploit the system's full kinematic capability. Doing so, however, requires a hydrodynamic model and derivatives throughout the prediction horizon. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) captures geometry-dependent forces and moments for such a model, but is too expensive to evaluate online. We present a differentiable analytical hydrodynamic model combining smooth spherical-harmonic force and moment fields with a coupled added-inertia matrix identified from CFD. It compactly represents velocity and acceleration-dependent loads and provides their derivatives in closed form. These derivatives are propagated through free-floating vehicle--manipulator dynamics for whole-body trajectory optimization and receding-horizon control, jointly optimizing thruster forces and joint torques for reaching and continuous tracking. Held-out CFD tests validate the principal translational-force and rotational-moment fields and the added-inertia response. The analytical Jacobians evaluate faster and avoid the step-size sensitivity of central finite differences. Closed-loop Stonefish experiments demonstrate whole-body MPC in an independent marine simulator. By making geometry-dependent hydrodynamics directly available to gradient-based control, the model incorporates water forces and their sensitivities into motion allocation between the vehicle and arm, rather than treating them only as disturbances.

papers.title: Class-Conditional Conformal Triage for ICAO Face-Image Compliance under Class Imbalance
papers.abstract: Automated ICAO/ISO face-image compliance analysers provide criterion-level pass/fail decisions, yet these verdicts do not quantify uncertainty when deciding whether to accept, reject, or retake a photograph. We investigate conformal prediction as a triage layer for BioGaze, evaluating 14 compliance criteria on the synthetic TONO benchmark. Without retraining the analyser, we fit per-criterion logistic classifiers and compare marginal and label-conditional (Mondrian) conformal prediction with conventional abstention rules using subject-disjoint splits. Marginal conformal prediction achieved approximately 0.90 overall coverage but substantially under-covered violations, with a ten-partition mean of 0.37 for one criterion. The corresponding Mondrian means ranged from 0.89 to 0.92 across criteria. However, most of the reduction in criterion-level false positives came from the logistic layer (0.145 to 0.048), while tuned abstention rules achieved lower false-positive rates than Mondrian at comparable retake rates. Bonferroni correction for joint coverage across 14 criteria required retaking nearly all images. These findings show that class-conditional conformal prediction can achieve near-target empirical coverage for minority violation classes and reveal trade-offs between statistical coverage, classification performance, and retake requirements in multi-criterion face-image compliance assessment.

papers.title: MoRE: Mixture-of-Experts for Multi-Physics Robotic World Models
papers.abstract: A robotic world model should predict how objects evolve under robot actions and physical dynamics. While recent 3D world models have shown strong predictive capabilities, they still struggle with the heterogeneous dynamics arising from diverse object interactions. To address this in a unified framework, we decompose robotic interactions into distinct physical regimes and assign each to a specialized motion expert. We introduce MoRE, a 3D world model with a mixture of motion experts organized around rigid, deformable, and prehensile dynamics. This design enables a single model to capture diverse physical behaviors while preserving regime-specific priors. Trained on mixed simulation and real-world data, MoRE integrates with Model Predictive Control (MPC) to support diverse manipulation tasks. Experiments show that MoRE improves prediction accuracy across physics regimes, leading to stronger real-world MPC performance. Code, data, and project website are available at https://alwaysleepy.github.io/MoRE-WM-site/.

papers.title: Total Hip Arthroplasty on Tumor Treating Fields Delivery for Ovarian Carcinoma: A Finite Element Study
papers.abstract: Background: Tumor Treating Fields (TTFields) are being investigated for pelvic malignancies, while total hip arthroplasty (THA) is increasingly common. This study evaluated whether THA prosthetic materials influence TTFields distribution and target dosimetry in ovarian tumors. Methods: Patient-specific finite element models were generated from computed tomography datasets of four patients with ovarian carcinoma. Three-dimensional simulations assigned cortical bone, Ti6Al4V titanium alloy, Co28Cr6Mo cobalt-chromium alloy, or tantalum to both femurs or to a single femur. Electric field (E), specific absorption rate (SAR), and current density (CD) were quantified in the clinical target volume (CTV), femur, and skin using 95%, 50%, and 5% volume-based metrics. Results: Bilateral implant properties produced minor CTV dosimetric changes, with mean and median percent differences generally within ±3.4% across metrics. Tantalum closely approximated cortical bone, typically within ±1%. Implants substantially reduced femoral E and SAR distributions while increasing CD. Skin exposure decreased modestly across 95% and 50% volumes. Unilateral implants similarly preserved CTV dosimetry within ±5.8%, while the contralateral cortical femur changed by less than 3.2%. Conclusions: In our preliminary analysis, THA materials altered femoral distributions of TTFields while largely preserving relevant CTV dosimetry in both bilateral and unilateral configurations. Tantalum closely approximated cortical bone and produced slightly greater skin reductions.

papers.title: Analysis of mechanical properties and corrosion behavior of Ti-6Al-4 V cellular scaffolds (BCC, SHC, CCP) fabricated using PBF-LB/M process
papers.abstract: Biomedical implants with scaffold structures are required to ensure osseointegration and mechanical stability. The aim of this study was to design and analyse selected mechanical and microstructural properties of 3D scaffold structures made of Ti-6Al-4 V titanium alloy for biomedical applications. Three different unit cells with various topologies were considered. The designed unit cells were used to create 3D scaffold structures using a Powder Bed Fusion – Laser Beam/Metal process. The obtained computer topography scans allow for a comparison of the deviations of the 3D printed structures with the intended geometry. The morphology of the obtained structures was analysed via scanning electron microscopy, their chemical composition was explored using energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy, their mechanical strength was obtained via compression testing, and their corrosion resistance was investigated using the potentiodynamic polarisation method. The strength of the scaffold structure was found to be greater when the printing direction coincided with the loading direction during compression testing. A structure composed of spherical hollow cubic unit cells demonstrated the highest compressive strength. A scanning electron microscopy analysis revealed relationships between the topology of the structures, the excess material and unbound Ti-6Al-4 V particles present in the selective laser melted structure. The scaffold structures were characterised by greater corrosive activity and greater susceptibility to corrosive processes compared to the solid Ti-6Al-4 V sample.

papers.title: Analysis of the postoperative mechanical properties of PEEK bone plates in a distal femoral fracture model
papers.abstract: Distal femoral fractures suffer high complication risks induced by stress shielding of high-modulus titanium locking plates. This work aimed to compare the biomechanical performance of four PEEK-series plates and titanium alloy implants for distal femoral fracture fixation, and establish material selection strategy. A Sawbones synthetic femur was fabricated into a comminuted fracture model. Four locking plates including pure PEEK, toughened CFR-PEEK, layered anisotropic PEEK and titanium alloy were analyzed via finite element simulation and 1000 N axial compression tests. Results showed that structural stiffness saturated at 20–110 GPa: modulus elevation from 6 to 20 GPa brought 28.4% stiffness improvement, while modulus increasing to 110 GPa only gained extra 9.8% stiffness. Toughened CFR-PEEK presented structural stiffness similar to titanium plates (femoral head displacement: 0.75 mm vs 0.69 mm), and lower stress shielding (peri-fracture bone stress: 40.2 MPa vs 30.9 MPa). Layered anisotropic PEEK suffered excessive plate stress (683.5 MPa) and unstable deformation, while pure PEEK lacked bearing capacity. In conclusion, toughened CFR-PEEK with elastic modulus above 20 GPa is a qualified substitute for titanium plates, which can balance fixation stability and stress shielding reduction for distal femoral fracture treatment. The research results propose a new approach to selecting bone plate materials: for isotropic materials, selecting an elastic modulus within the stiffness saturation range can achieve mechanical properties comparable to those of traditional metal bone plates while mitigating the stress shielding effect; for anisotropic materials, improving flexural strength can enhance structural stiffness while also mitigating the stress shielding effect.

papers.abstract: Infill patterns for load-bearing printed parts are often chosen with little evidence, and a homogenised finite-element model calibrated from the slicer toolpath is the natural screening tool. We measured where such a model stops being reliable, using a topology-optimised Messerschmitt–Bölkow–Blohm beam with cubic, gyroid and honeycomb infill at two densities. The reference is a road-resolved model of every deposited toolpath; no beam was tested mechanically. Three limits appear. First, inputs: skipping arc moves without updating the position inflates the gyroid orientation input in all four slicers tested, and the nominal density setting hides almost all of the pattern difference. Second, the core law: a scalar density law falls 8 to 20% below the reference and loses the difference between cubic and gyroid, while a homogenised tensor removes this error. Third, resolution: with a tensor core and dense material of the correct thickness, stiffness agrees with the reference within 5 to 7%, yet cubic and honeycomb cannot be separated. Omitting the solid layers about halves the stiffness. Weaker bonding between layers keeps the pattern order. These results apply to one beam and to linear elasticity. The data and code are openly available.

papers.title: Transient heat transfer characteristics and multi-objective optimization of HTGR thermal insulation cavity based on an iterative thermal network
papers.abstract: The thermal protection design of the internal insulation cavity is crucial for the drive motor of a High-Temperature Gas-Cooled Reactor (HTGR) under extreme thermal shocks. Nonetheless, the insulation flange, as the core component of this cavity, exhibits an inherent physical constraint between its steady-state thermal insulation and transient thermal shock resistance, making it difficult to satisfy both protection requirements through single-dimensional design. Moreover, the traditional three-dimensional Finite Volume Method (FVM) entails prohibitive computational costs during multi-constraint structural optimization, failing to meet the demands of large-scale parametric design. Given this issue, with the HTGR insulation cavity as the research object, a multi-objective collaborative optimization method is established based on the Transient Thermal Network Model (TNM) and extreme value normalization theory. First, a TNM reduced-order model of the flange and insulation components is constructed using the lumped parameter method, followed by the validation of its accuracy in transient heat transfer calculations against limited FVM simulations. On this basis, the steady-state total temperature difference and the maximum transient temperature change rate are extracted as evaluation indicators. Through extreme value normalization, the dimensional impact is eliminated to construct a comprehensive evaluation objective function that considers both steady-state and transient protection performance. This model enables parametric optimization of the axial height of the insulation ring under an equal-volume constraint, revealing the nonlinear influence law of structural dimensions on the comprehensive evaluation index. The results demonstrate that the comprehensive evaluation index achieves its optimal value when the axial height of the insulation ring is near 93.2 mm. At this point, the comprehensive thermal protection performance of the flange achieves an optimal thermal balance. The maximum error between this optimal solution and the FVM calculation results is 6.14% according to cross-validation. This study effectively reduces the computational cost of complex heat transfer processes. The established modeling and optimization framework provides methodological support for the design of HTGR thermal protection structures while exhibiting significant theoretical value and broad engineering applicability. It can be widely applied to other multi-component equipment featuring complex geometries and multi-dimensional heat transfer coupling that are suitable for efficient reduced-order thermal analysis using the thermal network model.

papers.title: Parametric design selection and ambient experimental assessment of a beryllium-copper spiral flexure spring for long-life Stirling cryocooler compressors
papers.abstract: Free-piston Stirling cryocoolers require flexure suspensions that combine low axial stiffness, high radial stiffness, modal separation, manufacturability and long cyclic endurance. This study reports a constrained, one-factor-at-a-time parametric screening procedure for a three-arm spiral flexure disc, followed by ambient experimental assessment of the selected design. Six candidate alloys (AISI 302, AISI 304, Be-Cu C17000, Be-Cu C17200 TH, Ti-6Al-4V and AMPCOLOY® 944) and five geometric variables (arm count, spiral-cut width, sweep angle, disc thickness and disc diameter) were screened using nonlinear static structural, modal and stress-life finite element analyses in ANSYS® Workbench, with photo-etch manufacturability treated as a hard feasibility constraint. The selected configuration was Be-Cu C17200 TH, three arms, 0.6 mm cut width, 0.7 mm disc thickness, 560° sweep, 69 mm diameter and ±5 mm design stroke. For the selected design, analytical, numerical and experimental axial stiffness values were 1495.00, 1451.45 and 1460.25 N/m, respectively; the three routes agreed within 3%, while FEA and experiment differed by 0.6%. Measured and predicted strain agreed within 3%–7% across the stroke. An ambient fatigue campaign reached 100,755,000 fully reversed cycles at ±5 mm and 50 Hz without detected crack initiation, exceeding the adopted 10 8 -cycle run-out criterion by 0.76%. This result is a run-out at one stress level rather than a statistical infinite-life demonstration. Cryogenic mechanical qualification, direct radial-stiffness measurement, and a formal global multi-objective optimisation remain outside the present evidence base.

papers.title: Predictive numerical modelling of dynamic behaviour in damaged 3D-printed ABS/PLA composite plates
papers.abstract: Finite-element modelling has been widely used to analyse the influence of damage on structural dynamic responses. Existing studies have predominantly focused on traditional isotropic materials or idealized damage geometries, while its application to complex additively manufactured structures, including three-dimensional (3D)-printed polymer composites with inherent anisotropy and geometric complexity, remains limited. Recent efforts have incorporated thermomechanical coupling and experimental validation to improve prediction accuracy, yet many models still overlook material anisotropy and geometric intricacies specific to additive manufacturing. This study systematically investigates the effects of crack length, angle and position on the dynamic response of 3D-printed acrylonitrile butadiene styrene/polylactic acid composite plates using finite-element simulation, experimental testing and machine learning. A high-fidelity parametric model was developed in COMSOL Multiphysics® under cantilever boundary conditions. The results show that increasing crack length monotonically reduces natural frequencies, with higher-order modes being more sensitive. Crack angles between 0° and 90° cause nonlinear stiffness degradation associated with the alignment between the crack and vibration stress direction, while crack-location effects depend on proximity to regions of high strain energy. Experimental validation shows trends consistent with the simulations, with errors controlled within 10%. In addition, a Deep Q-Network model was used to predict frequency changes caused by crack parameters, achieving 99.9% accuracy. The study provides a reproducible workflow for damage modelling of printed composites, clarifies the influence of crack geometry on dynamic behaviour, supports vibration-based damage assessment and integrates finite-element analysis with reinforcement learning for structural parameter regression, with theoretical and practical value.

papers.title: Modeling Glioblastoma Dynamics Using an Engineered Bioprinted Model of Glioma Stem Cell Spheroids
papers.abstract: Introduction Glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) is among the most lethal primary brain tumors, with a median survival of approximately 15 months. Progress has been limited in part by the lack of physiologically relevant in vitro models that recapitulate the three-dimensional (3D) architecture, cellular heterogeneity, and microenvironmental complexity of human tumors. Here, we aimed to develop a patient-derived 3D GBM spheroid platform to investigate tumor cell dynamics. Methods Spheroids generated from patient-derived glioma stem cells (GSC) were examined for outgrowth, stemness-associated and lineage-associated markers as well as culture-associated differences in protein abundance. Spheroids were co-cultured with endothelial cells to examine tumor-endothelial interactions. To enhance spatial organization, spheroids were embedded within engineered hydrogels and incorporated into constructs using extrusion-based 3D bioprinting. Printed constructs were evaluated for spheroid morphology, viability, and metabolic activity. Results The examined proneural GSC type exhibited greater peripheral outgrowth than the mesenchymal type. Spheroids exhibited stemness-associated and lineage-associated markers, while quantitative proteomic profiling identified culture-associated differences in proteins related to cell-cell adhesion and metabolism. Printed constructs retained gross spheroid morphology and showed evidence of cell survival and metabolic activity. Qualitative imaging showed cellular projections and reduced separation between GSC and endothelial cell populations over time. Conclusions This integrated 3D spheroid and bioprinting platform provides a framework for investigating tumor-endothelial interactions. Further replication, matched controls, and functional validation will be needed to support mechanistic studies and future therapeutic evaluation in GBM. Graphic Abstract Patient-derived glioma stem cell spheroids are characterized under distinct culture conditions to examine outgrowth, marker expression, and proteomic profiles, while their spatially patterned bioprinting with endothelial cells enables qualitative observation of cellular organization over time.

papers.title: The “Double-Hybrid” Strategy for Complex Primary Total Knee Arthroplasty Using a Varus–Valgus Constrained Insert and Standard Cementless Femoral Component
papers.abstract: Background Varus–valgus constrained (VVC) inserts are increasingly used in complex primary total knee arthroplasty (TKA) when additional coronal plane stability is required. Because increased constraint increases mechanical stress, VVC constructs are traditionally combined with cemented stemmed femoral and tibial components. In parallel, cementless fixation in primary TKA has shown excellent survivorship and osseointegration. A construct combining a cementless posterior-stabilized (PS) femoral component with a cemented stemmed VVC tibial construct may enhance stability while preserving bone stock. Outcomes of this "double-hybrid" strategy remain unreported. Methods We retrospectively reviewed 45 complex primary TKAs in 40 patients at a single institution (2021-2025). Mean age was 64.9 ± 13.0 years, and median body mass index (BMI) was 30.6 kg/m 2 (interquartile range (IQR) 26.1-32.9). All procedures used a medial parapatellar approach, mechanical alignment, and the same implant combination: cementless PS femoral component with cemented tibial Universal Baseplate, short stem, and VVC insert. Outcomes included radiolucencies, aseptic loosening, instability or revision. Results At a median follow-up of 27 months (IQR 23-46), no mechanical failures, radiolucencies, or aseptic loosening occurred. Functional outcomes and patient-reported outcome measures improved significantly. HKA alignment improved significantly in both varus and valgus knees. No instability or revision occurred. Conclusions This "double-hybrid" construct demonstrated favorable short-term outcomes in complex primary TKA. The combination of a cementless PS femoral component with a cemented stemmed VVC tibial construct provided reliable stability without early failure or loosening. It may represent a bone-preserving option when increased constraint is required. Longer-term follow-up is needed to confirm durability.

papers.title: Modern implantological alloys and high-entropy materials: comparative characteristics of mechanical, chemical and biocompatible properties
papers.abstract: Relevance: Despite progress in implantology, modern materials (titanium, cobalt-chrome alloys, stainless steel) have a number of disadvantages: high modulus of elasticity leading to "stress shielding", risk of corrosion and potential cytotoxicity of alloying elements. This determines the active search for new biocompatible materials, among which high-entropy alloys (HEAs) are a promising direction. Review purpose: To conduct a comparative analysis of the mechanical, chemical and biological properties of classical implant alloys and new HEAs to assess the potential of the latter as biomaterials. Conclusions: The literature analysis demonstrates that although titanium alloys remain the "gold standard" in implantology, certain HEA compositions (such as TiZrHfNbTaMo, CrMoNbTiZr) possess a unique combination of properties. These include low modulus of elasticity (close to bone tissue), high corrosion resistance, excellent in vitro biocompatibility and the ability to impart antibacterial properties due to the "cocktail effect". Thus, HEAs represent a promising class of materials for creating a new generation of implants. However, for their introduction into clinical practice, further comprehensive research is needed, especially preclinical in vivo studies investigating the entire spectrum of properties necessary for implantology.Keywords: high-entropy alloys (HEA), biocompatibility, dental implantology, modulus of elasticity, corrosion resistance, biomaterials, literature review.

papers.title: Design and compressive behavior of 3D-printed PA6/CF torsional-antagonistic metamaterials
papers.abstract: By leveraging the unique kinematic characteristics of compression-torsion coupled structures, this study proposes a novel compression-torsion mechanical metamaterial featuring an internal antagonistic mechanism, termed AKLS. To achieve efficient fabrication of this complex lattice structure, the fused deposition modeling (FDM) 3D printing process was employed due to its cost-effectiveness and high compatibility with lattice configurations. To accurately capture the unique mechanical anisotropy induced by the FDM process, an engineering adaptation of a transversely isotropic constitutive model was employed to characterize the printed specimens. This tailored approach was implemented via a custom dynamic explicit user material subroutine (VUMAT), enabling reliable finite element predictions of the compressive deformation process. Quasi-static compression tests and numerical simulations reveal that, compared to the conventional compression-twist lattice (CCTL), the designed AKLS exhibits substantial advantages in energy absorption. papers.title: A COMPREHENSIVE SYSTEMATIC REVIEW COMPARING FUNCTIONAL OUTCOMES OF CEMENTED VERSUS UNCEMENTED FIXATION IN TOTAL HIP ARTHROPLASTY IN PATIENTS WITH OSTEOPOROSIS
papers.abstract: Introduction: Osteoporosis is present in ±25% of total hip arthroplasty (THA) patients, yet most are undiagnosed. Uncemented fixation depends on press-fit stability in deficient bone, whereas cement provides immediate stability. Comparative effectiveness in the osteoporotic population has not been systematically established. Methods: The study strictly adhered to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis (PRISMA) 2020 guidelines. Eligible: RCTs, cohorts, case-control, cross-sectional, and registry studies. Thirteen outcome domains narratively synthesised; GRADE and exploratory ROC performed. Results: Twenty-seven studies (3,063,390 procedures): 5 RCTs, 3 prospective cohorts, 17 retrospective/registry cohorts, 1 case-control, 1 cross-sectional. Cemented fixation consistently reduced periprosthetic femoral fracture: WHiTE 5 (0.5% vs 2.1%; OR uncemented 4.37; 95%CI 1.19–24.00); Japan (OR 0.40; 0.30–0.53). Registry: fracture revision 6–7× higher with cementless. Early function favoured cement (HHS 4 months 78.0 vs 70.7; EQ-5D 0.68 vs 0.53), dissipated by 24–48 months. Residual pain at 1 year lower with cement (23.6% vs 34.4%). Osteoporosis (T≤−2.5) increased fracture (6.5% vs 1.0%) and revision (7.5% vs 1.5%). ROC: multivariable model AUC 0.874; osteoporosis 0.774; fixation 0.717–0.761. Anti-osteoporosis pharmacotherapy reduced fracture HR 0.50 (0.39–0.65). 10-year survivorship ≥75 years: cemented 95.9% vs uncemented 93.0%. GRADE: moderate for fracture, low-moderate for early function, low for satisfaction. Discussion: Cement's main benefit is mechanical—eliminating dependence on deficient bone. The functional advantage is real but time-limited, mediated by fracture and pain prevention. Contemporary evidence modifies the dichotomy: stem geometry and collar modify risk independently of cement. Cement concerns (bone-cement implantation syndrome, early male mortality) remain relevant. Conclusion: In osteoporosis, cemented fixation is the default strategy, providing significant periprosthetic fracture reduction, superior early function, and less pain, at the cost of longer operative time and a small early mortality signal. Functional scores converge in the medium term—the main argument for cement is fracture prevention. Recommendations: pre-operative DXA in age ≥70 years; default cement if T≤−2.5 or Dorr C; use collared/composite-beam designs if cementless; initiate post-operative anti-osteoporosis therapy.

papers.title: Preemptive solving of future problems: Multitask Preplay in humans and machines
papers.abstract: Humans can pursue a near-infinite variety of tasks, but typically can only pursue a small number at the same time. We hypothesize that humans leverage experience on one task to preemptively learn solutions to other tasks that were accessible but not pursued. We formalize this idea as “Multitask Preplay”, an algorithm that replays experience on one task as the starting point for “preplay”—counterfactual simulation of an accessible but unpursued task. Preplay is used to learn a predictive representation that can support fast, adaptive task performance later on. When implemented within deep reinforcement learning, it predicts human generalization to novel tasks more accurately than traditional planning and predictive representation methods across grid-worlds and a 2D Minecraft domain. Additionally, Multitask Preplay improves an artificial agent’s ability to generalize to new environments sharing task co-occurrence structure. These findings demonstrate that Multitask Preplay is a scalable theory of human counterfactual learning and generalization; endowing artificial agents with this capacity can significantly improve their performance in challenging multitask environments.

papers.abstract: We present a Gaussian process emulator for estimating fast surface temperature response patterns to a range of different climate forcing agents, including both long-lived greenhouse gases and short-lived pollutants such as aerosols. This emulator is trained on simulations driven by perturbations to emissions (for short-lived pollutants) and concentrations (for long-lived greenhouse gases) using a full-complexity global climate model and predicts the response in the first five years after the forcing, at a small fraction of the computational cost. We outline the emulator design, including the choice of pollutant perturbations and the input space covered by the training data. We show that the emulator performs well in most regions of the chosen input space, except under very large aerosol perturbations. A global sensitivity analysis is carried out to characterize and understand emission-response relationships for each pollutant. We find similar large-scale patterns of sensitivity to aerosol pollutants released in different regions. Our work demonstrates the potential for rapid climate change projections subject to various climate forcing agents, focusing on the short-term response. This paves the way for the future development of more policy-relevant emulators, that can target decadal and multi-decadal timescales.

papers.title: Structure‐Aware Bayesian Full Waveform Inversion via Diffusion‐Regularized Stein Variational Gradient Descent
papers.abstract: Full waveform inversion (FWI) is a powerful tool for high‐resolution subsurface model reconstruction, but it remains highly nonlinear and ill‐posed, especially when the initial model is inaccurate or the acquired data are noisy and incomplete. Annealed Stein variational gradient descent (ASVGD) provides a particle‐based Bayesian framework for FWI by approximating the posterior distribution with an ensemble of velocity models, thereby enabling uncertainty quantification beyond a single deterministic solution. However, conventional ASVGD‐FWI commonly relies on simple handcrafted priors, such as Gaussian or smoothing assumptions, which are often insufficient to represent complex geological structures. To address this limitation, we introduce a learned diffusion model (DM) as an implicit regularization mechanism within the ASVGD‐FWI framework. Instead of explicitly evaluating the diffusion prior density, the trained DM acts as a learned geological projection operator that guides updated particles toward the distribution of plausible velocity models. In this way, the proposed method combines data consistency from FWI, posterior diversity from ASVGD, and structural realism from the diffusion prior. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the diffusion‐regularized ASVGD‐FWI produces more geologically consistent mean models, suppresses nonphysical artifacts, and yields uncertainty estimates that are more concentrated around structurally complex and poorly constrained regions. These results suggest that learned diffusion priors can effectively enhance Bayesian FWI by improving both inversion stability and the interpretability of posterior uncertainty.

papers.title: Uncertainty quantification reveals the limits of lattice thermal conductivity prediction
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of lattice thermal conductivity (κ L ) drives thermoelectric materials discovery, yet existing machine learning models rarely quantify the reliability of their predictions. Here, we use evidential neural networks to quantify predictive uncertainty and split it into aleatoric uncertainty (data noise) and epistemic uncertainty (model ignorance). Our analysis reveals that predictions of very low lattice thermal conductivity are inherently unreliable as aleatoric noise dominates the uncertainty, and this noise can rival or even exceed the predicted value itself. High-κ L materials, by contrast, carry higher epistemic uncertainty, indicating room for improvement by additional training data. Consistent with this observation, adding out-of-distribution samples improves model accuracy by reducing model uncertainty. We further develope an uncertainty-aware screening method that prioritizes predictions with low total uncertainty rather than relying solely on the absolute value of κ L . This approach recovers a wide range of compositional classes with low κL from the Starrydata experimental repository at nearly twice the rate of random selection, thereby narrowing the search space needed to identify promising materials. These results establish evidential neural networks as a practical uncertainty-aware tool for κ L prediction, enabling reliable candidate screening and guiding data-collection to accelerate materials discovery.

papers.title: Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Biot's Model via Fixed-Stress Splitting and Energy Natural Gradient Descent
papers.abstract: Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) have recently gained considerable attention as a mesh-free framework for solving partial differential equations. Nevertheless, their performance deteriorates when applied to strongly coupled multiphysics systems, such as Biot’s consolidation model, due to severely ill-conditioned optimization landscapes. In this work, we propose a robust PINN-based solver, termed FS-ENGD-PINN, which synergistically integrates physics-based decoupling with geometry-aware optimization. Specifically, the Fixed-Stress (FS) splitting scheme is employed to decompose the coupled poroelastic system into contractive mechanics and flow subproblems, thereby significantly improving training stability and convergence. To further accelerate optimization, we adopt Energy Natural Gradient Descent (ENGD), which approximates the Newton direction in function space effectively mitigates stiffness-induced slow convergence. Moreover, to address volumetric locking arising in the nearly incompressible regime, we incorporate a three-field mixed formulation with an additional total pressure variable into the PINN framework. Extensive numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed FS-ENGD-PINN consistently outperforms standard PINN formulations in terms of accuracy and robustness, providing a unified and reliable learning-based solver for poroelasticity across a wide range of material parameters.

papers.title: A closed-loop data-driven framework for value stream mapping and future-state design
papers.abstract: Value Stream Mapping (VSM) is widely used in Lean Manufacturing to identify waste and support continuous improvement, but conventional VSM relies on manual data collection, static process representations, and expert interpretation. This paper proposes a data-driven VSM/VSD decision-support framework that establishes a traceable path from operational event data to current-state reconstruction, process diagnosis, simulation-based evaluation, and future-state redesign. Process Mining reconstructs observed process behavior and supports quantitative current-state VSM generation; Complex Network Analysis characterizes structural dependencies; Explainable Machine Learning integrates operational and network-derived information to identify and interpret process criticalities; and Digital Twin simulation evaluates candidate improvement interventions before they are translated into Future-State Value Stream Designs. The framework was evaluated using a controlled synthetic manufacturing event log and three heterogeneous real-world event logs under a leakage-controlled temporal protocol. Network-derived features provided complementary predictive information beyond conventional operational variables, with the strongest gains observed for rework prediction: Random Forest F1-score increased from 0.2243 to 1.0000 for BPI2017 and from 0.4658 to 0.7451 for BPI2019. In the cumulative simulation-based evaluation, the complete framework reduced Lead Time by 32.40%, Work-In-Process by 45.09%, Defect Rate by 27.63%, and Rework Rate by 45.52%, while increasing Throughput by 71.73% relative to the baseline. The results support a reproducible transition from descriptive VSM toward evidence-based, quantitatively evaluated Future-State Value Stream Design.

To capture the latent relationships underlying this phenomenon, we develop a model-based clustering approach to group individuals in Italy on the basis of their digital skills. This is done by using a set of binary indicators on digital abilities collected from the 2021 edition of the “Aspects of Daily Life” survey administered by the Italian National Statistical Office. Methodologically, we extend the Mixture of Experts Latent Trait Analyzers (MELTA) model to handle complex survey designs. MELTA is a model-based clustering approach for multivariate binary data that integrates finite mixtures with multidimensional latent traits. It further allows modeling the impact of covariates on cluster allocation, on the conditional responses’ distribution, on both (as in standard mixtures of experts models), or on neither. To deal with survey data, MELTA is extended by formally incorporating sampling weights into both the estimation algorithm and the uncertainty quantification. The proposed framework enables the identification of population-level digital profiles in Italy, while also assessing the role of socio-demographic characteristics in cluster formation and digital skill usage in the target population.

papers.title: Comparative Analysis of Model Predictive Control Strategies for Microgrids with Integrated Hydrogen-Fuelled Microturbine Dynamics and Nonlinear Battery Models
papers.abstract: Hydrogen-fuelled microturbines can complement photovoltaic generation and battery storage in grid-connected microgrids, yet energy management formulations usually assume constant battery efficiencies, treat the hybrid inverter as an ideal interface and describe the dispatchable units through static limits. This paper embeds the three elements in a single mixed-integer linear model predictive controller: the efficiency surface identified from measurements on the battery modules and tabulated as a function of the state of charge and of the power, enters as an exact continuous piecewise-linear interpolation over a triangulation, with a unique value at every operating point; the balance of the hybrid inverter, including the charge of the battery from the grid, is imposed with mutually exclusive modes and conversion efficiency; and the start-up, shut-down and minimum up and down times of the electrolyser and of the microturbine form part of the commitment problem. Nine scenarios of the microgrid of the University of Seville, with measured demand and generation, are evaluated over a five-day window under an economic and an energy-oriented objective, each one with the measured surface and with constant efficiencies. The piecewise-linear model reduces the mean absolute error of the efficiency from 0.0731 to 0.0084 in charging and from 0.0711 to 0.0023 in discharging, the maximum error of the power surface from 27.51 % to 4.77 % of the inverter rating, and the accumulated energy error from violet 3.52–12.26 kWh to 0.185–0.676 kWh. The economic objective lowers the import cost by 4.29 % to 15.32 % with respect to the energy-oriented one, which imports 2.85 % to 13.85 % less energy, and the battery representation shifts the cost between −3.93 % and +7.19 % while the microturbine schedule stays stable.

papers.title: Physics-informed neural surrogates for joint spent-fuel decay heat and pool thermal screening
papers.abstract: • Includes a 20,000-case spent-fuel decay heat and pool thermal response benchmark. • Physics-informed networks penalize thermal and decay-heat inconsistencies. • Joint in-distribution normalized error is 52.2 % below the standard neural ensemble. • The selected model reaches 9.25 % mean absolute percentage error on calorimetry. Rapid spent fuel pool (SFP) assessment requires fast, reliable estimates of decay heat and thermal response across heterogeneous fuel inventories and degraded cooling states. This study establishes a new, reproducible benchmark by sampling three-cohort pressurized water reactor spent-fuel inventories, deriving decay heat from an open Serpent2 depletion library, and propagating the resulting heat load through a reduced-order subcooled pool energy balance. The proposed physics-informed neural network (PINN) embeds heat-balance consistency, physically correct transient direction, and decay-heat monotonicity into supervised learning. These constraints directly couple the heat-load and temperature targets and discourage physically inconsistent predictions under domain shift. To the authors’ knowledge, this is the first openly reproducible study to evaluate a problem-specific PINN for joint SFP decay-heat and bulk-temperature prediction using independent calorimetry and explicit domain-shift tests. The latter is compared on independent and identically distributed (IID) and domain-shift conditions with engineering and statistical baselines, multilayer perceptron (MLP) ensembles, physics-feature MLPs and decay-heat residual hybrids. Architectures and hyperparameters are selected using validation scores; performance is assessed through repeated holdouts and external CLAB calorimetry. Direct Serpent interpolation achieves 5.65 % MAPE on 16 measured 17 × 17 CLAB assemblies, reduced to 1.73 % by the reported 27.1 W bias correction. Across five random seeds, the selected PINN MLP attains an IID mean normalized RMSE of 0.031, reducing IID mean normalized RMSE by 52.2 % relative to the standard MLP ensemble, while achieving 9.25 % external decay-heat MAPE. The results demonstrate that problem-specific physics constraints materially improve rapid, simultaneous heat-load and thermal-response prediction.

papers.title: Practice Teachers’ Perspectives on Peer-Led Learning with Social Work Students on Placement in Northern Ireland
papers.abstract: Background: Peer-led learning can facilitate collaborative knowledge development, provide support and contribute to the formation of professional social work identity. Practice teachers play a pivotal role in supervising, assessing and supporting skills development, integrating social work theory and values into competent practice. The Peer Learning Bubble Model (PLBM), developed in 2020, communicates a four-domain framework to support these activities and is centred on belonging within a community of practice. This research builds on findings from students’ experiences by critically examining the pilot implementation of the PLBM in practice learning opportunities, drawing on facilitators’ reflections and experiences. Methods: A two-stage qualitative design was employed; PLBM facilitators were recruited using snowball sampling. Stage One utilized semi-structured interviews (n = 3), informed by Constructivist Grounded Theory, and Stage Two employed critical autoethnographic accounts (n = 3). Findings: PLBM provides a collaborative learning environment through reflective dialogue, active learning pedagogies and the co-construction of knowledge which challenges the power dynamics inherent in the practice teacher–student relationship. Conclusions: Overall, the PLBM supports facilitators and practice teachers to create learning environments where social work students can collaborate, critically reflect and learn about anti- oppressive practice and social justice, whilst developing the critical, relational and professional capabilities required for competent social work practice.

papers.title: Defect-tolerant and site-specific heterogeneity engineering in laser powder bed fusion metallic alloys
papers.abstract: Laser powder bed fusion (L-PBF) has moved from a shape-making technology toward a platform for local microstructure design. The extremely high thermal gradient, repeated remelting and rapid solidification make the process sensitive to defects, residual stress and anisotropy. These features were once treated mainly as manufacturing problems. Recent studies show that the same features can also be used to create designed heterogeneity across interfaces, grains, phases and crystallographic textures. This review discusses L-PBF from the perspective of defect-tolerant and site-specific heterogeneity engineering. Instead of separating the field into multi-material fabrication, in situ alloying and parameter control, the present review focuses on how different strategies redirect failure, suppress cracking, refine grains and assign local properties inside a single build. Particular attention is paid to interfacial bonding in dissimilar alloys, inoculation-assisted grain refinement in steels and aluminium alloys, scan-strategy-induced texture control and auxiliary-field-assisted melt-pool regulation. The review also highlights several unresolved issues, including the lack of reliable interfacial fracture metrics, the difficulty of linking local microstructure to component-scale service behaviour and the limited transferability of process windows between alloy systems. A defect-tolerant design framework is finally proposed for future L-PBF alloys.

papers.title: BCTBM: A Bottom-Current-Fused Two-Stage BM-mRMR Method for Seafloor Sediment Classification
papers.abstract: Seafloor sediment classification is critical for benthic habitat mapping and marine environmental protection. Existing classification methods mostly adopt seafloor surface observation parameters such as backscatter and bathymetry. These parameters only characterize surface seabed properties and lack physical prior information related to sediment formation mechanisms, which limits classification accuracy and physical interpretability. Considering that bottom-current kinetic energy (BCKE) governs sediment erosion, transport and deposition and further shapes the spatial distribution of sediments, this paper proposes a bottom-current-fused two-stage Bayesian MIC-augmented mRMR (BCTBM) architecture for seafloor sediment classification. BCTBM combines BCKE with acoustic and topographic features to construct a 77-dimensional multi-source feature set. Samples with high class separability are selected using the Jeffries–Matusita (J-M) distance, and a two-stage feature selection algorithm is further developed. ReliefF is first applied for coarse-grained feature screening to generate a candidate feature set; subsequently, the Bayesian MIC-augmented Minimum Redundancy Maximum Relevance (BM-mRMR) model employs Bayesian optimization (BO) to adaptively solve the optimal relevance–redundancy trade-off weights for seven target dimensions, and mRMR finally derives the optimal feature set based on the obtained optimal weights. The proposed method is validated in the shallow-water sediment classification scenario of the eastern English Channel. Eighty-four comparative experiments demonstrate that introducing BCKE improves the overall accuracy by 3.48% on average, with a maximum increment of 9.4%. The proposed two-stage BM-mRMR method achieves average accuracy improvements of 4.84% and 6.08% over ReliefF and ReliefF-mRMR, respectively. The classification results are consistent with the Hjulström–Sundborg sedimentary-dynamic framework, offering an effective pathway for refined benthic habitat mapping.
