papers.abstract: Background: This study investigates the potential of lattice structures in metal-ceramic frameworks for dental prostheses. Metal-ceramic restorations, used in both implant-supported and tooth-supported applications, often suffer from excessive weight due to their solid structure. Additive manufacturing offers a solution by enabling the creation of lightweight, complex internal geometries. This research comparatively analyzes re-entrant, strut-based, and triply periodic minimal surfaces lattice geometries in the pontic region of 3-unit metal-ceramic frameworks. The study focuses on manufacturability and mechanical strength, evaluating the resistance to compression values of different lattice forms. Methods: The study offers innovation by utilizing 7 different forms from 3 distinct lattice groups in dental frameworks using cobalt–chromium alloys. The research process involves scanning, laser powder bed fusion production, compression tests, and scanning electron microscope deformation analysis. Compression tests were performed at displacement levels of 0.5 mm, 1.0 mm, and 1.5 mm. For statistical data analysis, a 2-way analysis of variance test was used. The statistical significance level was determined as P <.05. Results: The solid control group demonstrated the highest compressive strength at all displacement levels, whereas TG3 showed the highest compressive strength among the lattice-integrated groups. While there was no significant difference between the other groups at the 0.5 mm compression test level (P >.05), significant differences were found between the other groups at the 1.0 and 1.5 mm levels (P <.001). Conclusion: It was determined that the investigated lattice structures and compression levels created significant differences between the groups, but the tested lattice geometries demonstrated promising mechanical behavior.

papers.title: Intelligent Vehicle Trajectory Tracking Control Based on Multi-Model-Switching Model Predictive Control
papers.abstract: Given the limited adaptability of conventional single-model model predictive control (MPC) to the complex driving conditions encountered by intelligent vehicles on varying road surfaces, as well as the trade-off between modeling accuracy and computational efficiency, this study proposes an adaptive multi-model-switching MPC strategy for trajectory tracking control. First, three prediction models with different levels of complexity are developed, including a kinematic model, a linear two-degree-of-freedom (2-DOF) dynamic model, and a nonlinear tire dynamic model. A model-switching mechanism based on vehicle speed, road curvature, and road-surface friction is then designed to select the appropriate prediction model according to the prevailing driving conditions. In addition, a lateral-deviation feedback correction strategy is introduced to further improve tracking accuracy and smooth the steering response. Finally, joint simulations using MATLAB/Simulink and CarSim are conducted under four representative driving scenarios. The results show that, compared with conventional single-model MPC, the proposed strategy effectively reduces lateral tracking errors and steering-angle fluctuations while maintaining favorable computational efficiency and vehicle stability. These results demonstrate the potential of the proposed method to achieve accurate and robust trajectory tracking for intelligent vehicles under complex and varying operating conditions.

papers.title: A Method for Optimizing Drilling Parameters Based on the Synergistic Optimization of Cost and Efficiency
papers.abstract: Adjusting drilling parameters affects both the rate of penetration (ROP) and drill bit wear, making ROP improvement alone an inadequate measure of overall drilling economics. However, incorporating the trade-off between drilling speed and the associated operating and wear costs into parameter optimization remains challenging. This study proposes a framework for jointly optimizing drilling cost and efficiency by integrating a Transformer–bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) model with multi-objective Bayesian optimization. The framework addresses nonlinear dependencies in drilling sequences and the propagation of prediction errors into parameter selection. Self-attention captures dependencies among sampling positions within the input window, while BiLSTM extracts sequential patterns to estimate ROP. WOB and RPM serve as decision variables, and time-dependent operating costs, energy costs, and bit wear costs are incorporated into cost per unit drilled length. A bi-objective optimization model accounts for predictive uncertainty and engineering constraints, while a rolling strategy recommends parameter ranges derived from near-optimal Pareto solutions. Experimental results show that Transformer-BiLSTM outperforms the LSTM, BiLSTM, and Transformer baselines across all three-evaluation metrics. The mean absolute error (MAE) and root mean square error (RMSE) are 0.5812 and 0.9408 m/h, respectively, with a coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.9515. In the case study of Well A in Block M, the joint optimization scheme increases the average ROP from 53.28 to 64.14 m/h, representing a 20.39% improvement. The number of bit replacements decreases from three to two. Compared with the scheme that optimizes ROP alone, the joint optimization scheme reduces total costs by 36.73%. It also achieves a higher drilling rate than the scheme that minimizes cost alone. By balancing ROP and operating costs, the proposed framework supports drilling parameter selection that jointly addresses drilling schedule requirements and economic objectives.

papers.title: BayeUNet-NLM: A Bayesian U-Net with Uncertainty-Guided Non-Local Means Post-Processing for Extreme Low-Light Denoising
papers.abstract: Extreme low-light image denoising, where photon shot noise and read noise dominate, remains a critical challenge for computer vision and computational photography. While deep learning models, particularly U-Net architectures, have shown remarkable performance, they often produce over-smoothed results and lack robust uncertainty quantification. This limitation is fundamentally rooted in the ill-posed, one-to-many nature of the low-light enhancement problem, which deterministic models fail to capture. This paper introduces BayeUNet-NLM, a novel two-stage framework that marries the representational power of a Bayesian deep network with the interpretable, structure-preserving capability of a classical denoiser. In the first stage, a Bayesian U-Net with Monte Carlo Dropout at test time generates both a denoised image and a per-pixel uncertainty map. This map quantifies the model's confidence, highlighting regions where data is ambiguous (e.g., due to extreme noise or missing textures). In the second stage, this uncertainty map is explicitly used to guide the classical Non-Local Means (NLM) post-processor, adaptively modulating its local bandwidth and its donor-reliability weights: high-uncertainty regions receive stronger non-local regularization from similar, more confident patches elsewhere in the image, while low-uncertainty regions are preserved. This synergy allows the model to recover fine details with high confidence while robustly denoising highly uncertain regions without introducing artifacts. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets (SID, LOL) demonstrate that BayeUNet-NLM outperforms the deep learning and traditional methods included in our comparison in both quantitative metrics (PSNR, SSIM) and qualitative visual quality, particularly in preserving textures and avoiding over-smoothing. Our work highlights the value of Bayesian uncertainty for guiding hybrid denoising pipelines.

papers.title: Multi-objective collaborative optimization of load-bearing and microwave absorption performance for graded octet-truss lattice sandwich structures
papers.abstract: The lack of reliable electromagnetic (EM) performance prediction models has long hindered the multifunctional design of lattice structures for integrated load-bearing and microwave absorption applications. This study proposed a systematic collaborative optimization framework for graded octet-truss lattice sandwich structures. First, the equivalent mechanical properties of the periodic unit cell were analytically derived via the matrix displacement method, establishing explicit analytical correlations between volume fraction and effective elastic parameters. Concurrently, full-wave simulations combined with an inversion algorithm was adopted to extract frequency-dependent equivalent EM parameters, and a high-precision random forest surrogate model was constructed for rapid EM response prediction. On this basis, a three-layer graded lattice core sandwich configuration was designed. Its load-bearing stiffness and microwave absorption capacity were characterized by higher-order shear deformation theory and transmission line theory, respectively. A multi-objective optimization model was established via the compromise programming method and solved by particle swarm optimization. Compared with the uniform counterpart, the optimized graded structure achieved a 34.96% increase in effective absorption bandwidth while maintaining structural stiffness, verifying the effectiveness of the proposed collaborative strategy.

papers.title: Finite-Horizon Performance Estimation for Online Parameter Refinement in RL–MPC Quadrupedal Locomotion
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning integrated with model predictive control (RL-MPC) enables adaptive quadrupedal locomotion, but learned controller parameters do not explicitly account for their subsequent closed-loop performance. This study proposes a finite-horizon performance estimator (FHPE) to guide online parameter refinement. Trained on rollout data, FHPE predicts the finite-horizon performance of local parameter candidates to guide constrained refinement of the nominal RL proposal. The refined parameters are implemented through MPC and Adaptive Impedance Modulation (AIM), while Transient Residual Compensation (TRC) regulates joint-level responses through spectral regularization and risk-dependent gating. Ablation studies show that FHPE-guided refinement reduces the combined performance cost by 12.68% compared with equal-budget search, while AIM and TRC improve execution performance and transient regulation. Robot performance evaluations demonstrate improved high-speed locomotion capability, an approximately 26% reduction in peak joint acceleration on uneven terrain, and an approximately 43% reduction in estimated mechanical work over 10 m on flat ground in hardware experiments. These findings suggest that finite-horizon performance prediction can improve online parameter selection, while joint-level adaptation helps translate refined parameters into effective locomotion control.

papers.title: Application of 3D-Printed Nanoparticle-Based Therapeutics in the Management of Diabetic Wounds: A Translational Approach
papers.abstract: Diabetic foot ulcers develop in an estimated 18.6 million people worldwide each year and precede most diabetes-related lower-extremity amputations. Three-dimensional (3D) printing has been combined with nanoparticle-based delivery to produce wound constructs that provide structural support while locally releasing antimicrobial, antioxidant, immunomodulatory, or pro-angiogenic agents. This narrative review examines nanoparticle-functionalized 3D-printed constructs for diabetic wound management from a manufacturing and materials perspective. It relates printing modality, bioink composition, scaffold architecture, nanoparticle loading and dispersion, and degradation and release behavior to reported biological outcomes, and summarizes the design, manufacturing features, and reported outcomes of the core studies. Preclinical studies, predominantly in streptozotocin-induced diabetic rodents, report accelerated wound closure, enhanced angiogenesis, antibacterial activity, and macrophage modulation relative to untreated or unloaded controls. However, models, comparators, endpoint definitions, and manufacturing reporting vary widely; few experiments separate the contribution of the nanoparticle from that of the printed architecture; and large-animal, long-term safety, and human data for nanoparticle-functionalized printed constructs remain scarce. Standardized human-relevant models, informative controls, reproducible quality-controlled manufacturing, and nanoparticle biodistribution studies are needed before clinical evaluation. Even at maturity, these constructs are best viewed as adjuncts to established diabetic foot care.

papers.title: Physics-informed deep learning of radiative MHD bioconvection in non-Newtonian hexa-hybrid nanofluids
papers.abstract: Purpose This examination explores the bioconvection flow of Casson-Williamson hexa-hybrid nanofluid (HEHNF) (Al₂O₃–CuO–SiO₂–ZnO–Fe₃O₄–TiO₂/H₂O) via an exponential stretchable, permeable vertical surface in a porous material. The model includes the effects of a magnetic field (MF), thermal buoyancy, thermal radiation, Brownian, thermophoretic diffusion, heat generation, viscous dissipation, Joule heating, chemical reaction, and gyrotactic motile microorganisms. Design/methodology/approach Similarity conversions reduce the managing equations to coupled non-linear ordinary differential equations (ODEs), which are solved with the MATLAB bvp4c routine and validated against published results for the limiting Williamson case. An artificial neural network trained with the Levenberg–Marquardt algorithm (ANN-LMA) and physics-informed neural networks (PINNs), which combines bvp4c data with equation and boundary residuals evaluated by automatic differentiation, are developed to predict the wall quantities. Findings The velocity declines with the magnetic, porosity, Casson, and Williamson parameters and increases with the Grashof number, while radiation, Brownian motion, thermophoresis, heat generation, and the Eckert number raise the temperature. Radiation weakens the wall temperature gradient, and the rise in the Nusselt number is due to the additional radiative heat flux. The concentration diminishes with the Schmidt number and the reaction parameter, and the microorganism density declines with the bioconvection Lewis and Peclet numbers, while the motile density number raises. The bvp4c results agree with published data to four decimal places, and in the limiting Williamson case the ANN-LMA and PINN skin friction coefficient (SFC) predictions differ from bvp4c by less than 1 0 ⁻ ³ . Originality/value The study presents a Casson–Williamson HEHNF bioconvective model with a combined numerical and machine-learning framework, in which the trained models act as fast substitutes for the solver in thermal and bioconvective transport applications.

papers.title: HCBF–HET–DMPC: Hierarchical event-triggered distributed model predictive control with hybrid control barrier functions for collision-free multi-agent navigation
papers.abstract: Addressing the real-time collision-free trajectory generation problem for large-scale multi-agent systems in dynamic interactive environments, this paper proposes a hierarchical event-triggered distributed model predictive control algorithm based on control barrier functions (HCBF–HET–DMPC). The algorithm constructs a hybrid CBF collision-avoidance strategy that integrates hard constraints at the first prediction step with soft constraints over the prediction horizon, thereby enforcing an unrelaxed safety constraint at the first prediction step and providing soft collision-avoidance guidance over the remaining prediction horizon. A risk-aware hierarchical event-triggered mechanism (ETM) dynamically switches solution modes on demand to prevent redundant computation. Built on a decoupled decentralised architecture, the algorithm uses distributed local optimisation based on shared predicted-trajectory information. Simulation results demonstrate that in large-scale, densely coupled multi-agent scenarios with up to 300 agents, HCBF–HET–DMPC substantially improves trajectory feasibility and the global agent completion rate. By avoiding unnecessary optimisation updates, the ETM preserves collision-avoidance performance while reducing optimiser activation and total computation time by more than 30%. The algorithm thus achieves a favourable balance among collision-avoidance safety, optimisation feasibility and computational efficiency for large-scale swarms.

papers.abstract: In this study, the mechanical, thermal, electrical, and piezoresistive performances of Gyroid lattice structures produced from multi-walled carbon nanotube (MWCNT)-reinforced PLA and ABS filaments using the fused filament fabrication (FFF) method were comparatively investigated. MWCNT was added to the PLA and ABS matrices at ratios of 3% and 5%, and Gyroid lattice-structured specimens with dimensions of 16 × 16 × 24 mm and wall thicknesses of 0.60, 0.80, and 1.00 mm were produced. The structural and thermal properties of the composites were evaluated through Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR), thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), differential thermal analysis (DTA), and differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) analyses, while their mechanical behavior was determined by uniaxial compression tests. Electrical conductivity and gauge factor variations were measured under compressive deformation, and their piezoresistive performance was analyzed. The results showed that increasing the wall thickness enhanced the compressive strength and structural stability of the Gyroid structures throughout deformation. The composites containing 5% MWCNT exhibited higher initial electrical conductivity; while the specimens produced using PLA reached higher conductivity values compared to those produced using ABS. In contrast, the highest low-strain piezoresistive sensitivity was obtained with the combination of 3% MWCNT-PLA and a 1.00 mm wall thickness. The 5% MWCNT-ABS specimens exhibited a more regular and stable gauge factor behavior over a wide strain range. The findings demonstrate that MWCNT-reinforced Gyroid lattice structures produced by FFF can be used as tunable and multifunctional piezoresistive structures that combine mechanical load-bearing capacity with deformation-sensing functionality.

papers.title: Hybrid YOLO–U-Net Framework for Uncertainty-Aware Brain Tumour Segmentation and Web-Based Visualisation of MRI Scans.
papers.abstract: Brain tumour segmentation is a challenging task in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) that demands precise boundary definition and correct understanding of automated delineation. This study introduces a novel YOLO–U-Net system that combines tumour localisation, segmentation, uncertainty quantification and web-based visualisation. The method details an applied experimental design based on de-identified MRI scans, partitioning of patient-level data, intensity normalisation, resizing, and augmentation during training. YOLO detects the candidate tumour regions and U-Net generates the segmentation masks. Monte Carlo dropout makes multiple predictions to estimate uncertainty in detected regions. An original image, segmentation overlay and uncertainty maps are presented using a Streamlit interface. Evaluation is based on Dice similarity, intersection over union, precision, recall, calibration, error detection, and processing time. System comparisons resulted in Dice coefficients of 0.920 for the deterministic hybrid, and 0.917 for the uncertainty-aware hybrid. The stochastic pass performance was enhanced from 10 to 30, which resulted in an AUROC increase from 0.821 to 0.843 for the system error-detection problem, and inference time went from 2.40 to 4.80 seconds. These are synthetic values, testing for potential evaluation trade-offs and not testing for experimental effectiveness. The framework is a structured way to integrate segmentation and reliability information in an easy-to-use interface. Its accuracy, uncertainty quality, computational practicality and likely usefulness to support expert MRI review workflows will need to be determined through independent patient-level experiments, external validation, and usability assessment.

papers.title: Quasi-Static and High-Speed Compression of AlSi10Mg Menger Fractal Structures: An Interval-Dependent Experimental Assessment
papers.abstract: Laser powder bed fusion was used to fabricate first-, second-, and third-order (M1–M3) AlSi10Mg Menger structures. Sixty force–machine-displacement histories were obtained under quasi-static compression and nominal servo-hydraulic speeds of 5.4, 8.1, and 10 m/s, supported by quasi-static digital image correlation and high-speed images. Specific external work was evaluated over a common initial engineering strain of 4.66% (baseline A) and separately over order-specific minimum recorded high-speed strokes of 1.27, 5.69, and 17.74 mm (baseline B). Under baseline B, quasi-static specific work was 2.04, 11.80, and 39.16 J/g for M1–M3, respectively; these values reflect non-equivalent observation intervals. At the common strain, quasi-static work was 2.04, 1.63, and 1.02 J/g, versus 1.10, 1.77, and 1.19 J/g at 10 m/s. These are early-stage, machine-displacement-based comparisons, not measurements of complete crushing capacity. The short M1 high-speed interval and non-equivalent contact-zero procedures preclude interpreting its recorded work decrement as a validated material-rate effect. Corrected TOPSIS coefficients also depend on the evaluation interval and selected attributes, including a cross-regime consistency attribute with unresolved M1 uncertainty. The contribution is an experimentally bounded comparison of the tested as-built structures, rather than an unconditional order ranking or validated protection-design recommendation.

papers.title: Extrusion-based 3D bioprinting of soft carrot callus using an alginate-Laponite-methylcellulose hydrogel and quantification of secondary metabolites.
papers.abstract: Plant-based 3D bioprinting remains limited in its ability to regulate cell behavior and secondary metabolite production under well-defined structural conditions. In this study, we investigated the effects of scaffold geometry on plant cell function using an alginate-Laponite-methylcellulose hydrogel system. An optimized formulation enabled stable extrusion and the fabrication of reproducible porous and non-porous constructs containing non-genetically modified carrot callus. Here, we established a plant-focused extrusion bioprinting platform by defining the biofabrication window for this hydrogel system. Through systematic rheological characterization and printability analysis, a formulation composed of 3 wt% alginate, 6 wt% Laponite, and 6 wt% methylcellulose (3A6L6M) was identified as optimal for stable extrusion and cell encapsulation. Soft callus derived from hypocotyl tissue was generated using conventional tissue culture methods and used without genetic modification. Scaffold geometry influenced cell distribution, viability, and metabolic activity within the constructs. Porous scaffolds supported more uniform cell growth and exhibited significantly greater accumulation of carotenoid compounds than non-porous scaffolds. These differences may be attributable to improved nutrient diffusion and more uniform spatial organization of cells within the porous structure. Overall, this study identifies scaffold geometry as an important parameter influencing plant cell metabolism and demonstrates a simple, non-genetic strategy for structure-guided plant biofabrication.

papers.title: Preoperative Two-Step Test Performance Is Associated with Fast Walking at One Week After Total Hip Arthroplasty
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Early postoperative walking speed varies after total hip arthroplasty (THA), but its preoperative predictors remain unclear. This study aimed to determine whether preoperative physical performance and computed tomography (CT)-derived muscle parameters predict fast walking speed (≥1.0 m/s) one week after THA. Methods: We retrospectively evaluated 64 patients who underwent primary unilateral THA via a posterolateral approach. Maximum walking speed was assessed using a 10-m walk test at one week postoperatively, and patients were classified as fast (≥1.0 m/s; n = 26) or slow (<1.0 m/s; n = 38) walkers. Preoperative assessments included the two-step test (2ST), 30-s chair-stand test (CS-30), one-leg stance time, and CT-based assessments of hip muscle cross-sectional area and attenuation. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors of fast walking speed. Results: The fast-walking group showed better preoperative performance in the 2ST, CS-30, and one-leg stance time. CT-derived muscle parameters were largely comparable between groups. In multivariable analysis, the 2ST was the sole independent predictor of fast walking speed (per 0.1-unit increase: odds ratio, 1.61; 95% confidence interval, 1.09–2.38; p = 0.016). The optimal 2ST cutoff value was 0.977 (sensitivity, 73%; specificity, 76%), with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.78. Conclusions: Preoperative 2ST performance was independently associated with fast walking speed at one week after THA. A preoperative 2ST cutoff value of 0.977 may help identify patients likely to achieve this walking-speed threshold. Further studies should determine whether preoperative 2ST performance predicts longer-term functional outcomes after THA.

papers.title: Advances in nanomaterial-enhanced bioinks for bone tissue bioprinting
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional bioprinting provides a promising strategy for constructing living bone substitutes with controlled architecture, cellular organisation, and regenerative function. However, conventional hydrogel bioinks often struggle to simultaneously achieve sufficient printability, structural stability, and biological activity for bone tissue formation. The incorporation of nanomaterials has therefore emerged as an effective approach to transform hydrogel bioinks into multifunctional composite systems capable of regulating both material properties and the cellular microenvironment. This review first outlines the dynamic process of bone repair, including inflammation, tissue formation, vascularisation, and remodelling, and discusses the requirements that these biological processes impose on bioink design. Major bioprinting technologies, including extrusion-based, inkjet, light-based, coaxial, and embedded bioprinting, are then summarised with particular attention to their compatibility with nanomaterial-containing bioinks. The review subsequently focuses on ceramic nanomaterials, silicates and nanoclays, carbon-based nanomaterials, two-dimensional nanomaterials, and polymeric or fibrous nanomaterials. Their roles in regulating rheological behaviour, print fidelity, mechanical stability, mineralisation, osteogenic differentiation, angiogenesis, and immunomodulation are critically discussed. Current evidence demonstrates that nanomaterial performance is strongly dependent on particle composition, concentration, size, morphology, surface chemistry, dispersion state, and interactions with the surrounding polymer network. Increasing nanomaterial content does not necessarily improve regenerative outcomes and may instead compromise extrusion, photocrosslinking, cellular activity, or long-term structural stability. Future development should therefore move beyond empirical nanoparticle incorporation towards coordinated optimisation of nanomaterial properties, bioink formulation, printing parameters, cellular composition, and degradation behaviour. Such an integrated design framework may enable the development of next-generation bioinks capable of more closely recapitulating the dynamic and multicellular microenvironment required for functional bone regeneration.

papers.title: Discovering Novel Bracing Systems for Steel Box Girders with a Deep Reinforcement Learning Agent
papers.abstract: Steel trapezoidal box girder systems are highly susceptible to global lateral–torsional buckling (GLTB), a critical failure mode that typically occurs during concrete deck placement in the erection stage. Recent studies have introduced the partial top lateral bracing system (PTLBS), which places bracing exclusively at the end panels to provide warping restraint, as a more efficient alternative to the full top lateral bracing system for preventing GLTB. This paper presents an optimization framework that integrates deep reinforcement learning (DRL) with finite element analysis (FEA) to explore optimal top lateral bracing configurations for steel box girder systems. The DRL agent, guided by iterative FEA-based stability evaluations, seeks to minimize the number of bracing members while ensuring adequate GLTB resistance. papers.abstract: Stability of plate osteosynthesis depends not only on plate strength but also on the implant–screw junction. Screw loosening, thread stripping, plastic deformation of the shaft or hole failure can result in loss of fixation and revision. Ti-6Al-4V remains the standard alloy for extra-osseous plates, yet its elastic modulus is substantially higher than that of cortical bone and favors stress shielding. Carbon composites offer high specific strength, biocompatibility, radiolucency and a modulus closer to bone; they are already used for osteosynthesis and defect reconstruction. Comparative data on the strength of the implant–screw junction in carbon-composite versus titanium bodies under identical loading remain scarce. Aim. To compare failure modes of implant–screw junctions in Ti-6Al-4V and carbon-composite implants and to relate screw deflection to static load. Materials and methods. Junction strength was tested on a modified servohydraulic machine (maximum force 10 kN) in cantilever bending. Screws of different lengths with a conical head thread were inserted into a full-size titanium implant and into a composite-body model of the same wall thickness and hole diameter. The composite body was a Ukraine-manufactured carbon–carbon composite previously used for extra-osseous osteosynthesis. Each material–overhang combination was tested on at least five identical specimens (n ≥ 5). Load was applied to the free end of the screw at lever arms of 14-, 22- and 24-mm. Force and deflection were recorded; testing stopped after failure of the junction or of the implant body. Results. Mean relative strength of the composite implant–screw junction was 78 %. Failure modes differed: composite body failed by hole-rim crushing or plate fracture; titanium screws failed by plastic deformation. The conical threaded interface remained intact in every material and overhang tested. Indicative material-level ratio (composite junction capacity vs. published cortical bone strength) was approximately 4.4 versus 5.6 for titanium; this ratio is not a safety factor of a complete bone–implant construct. papers.abstract: Early-stage aircraft structural design choices strongly influence performance, yet preliminary sizing often relies on empirical methods which may be inaccurate for composite structures and unconventional layouts. A nested approach optimizes the number of ribs, number of stringers, and spar-cap width in an outer loop, while component sizing is handled by a commercial gradient-based solver in an inner loop. A staged multi-run sizing strategy reduces structural mass by up to 450 kg relative to the first feasible sizing result while reducing run-to-run variability. A Gaussian-process surrogate, trained on a limited number of sizing results, guides the outer-loop search with a noise-aware improvement-based acquisition function. Three Bayesian optimization repetitions were performed for each of three initial datasets, with 30 layout evaluations per study. All nine studies reduced the initial best mass, returning structural masses of 1735.62–1778.82 kg. The lowest mean mass was obtained with the largest allocation of the budget to adaptive sampling. Selected layouts typically featured 50 mm wide spar caps and 13–14 stringers, while rib counts varied. Results were benchmarked against a global gradient-free optimizer.

papers.title: Biodegradable magnesium alloys: Corrosion mechanisms, alloy design, surface treatment and emerging biomedical applications
papers.abstract: Biomedical implants increasingly require materials that combine mechanical reliability with controlled biodegradability and functional integration. Magnesium (Mg) alloys have attracted considerable attention as promising materials owing to their advantageous mechanical properties, excellent biocompatibility, and intrinsic degradability, which can eliminate secondary removal surgeries and reduce stress shielding through their bone-matching elastic modulus. However, their broader clinical application is constrained by rapid and complex corrosion behavior in physiological environments. The work systematically analyzes corrosion mechanisms, including electrochemical dissolution, unstable surface film formation, hydrogen evolution, and the negative differential effect, and evaluates competing models such as incomplete film, univalent Mg and catalytic activation theories. The influence of impurities and alloying elements is critically assessed, revealing the dominant roles of micro-galvanic effects and hydrogen evolution kinetics in governing degradation. To address these challenges, strategies including ultra-high purification, lean alloy design, and micro-alloying are proposed to achieve controlled corrosion while preserving mechanical integrity. The integration of computational approaches, including density functional theory, thermodynamic modeling, molecular dynamics, and machine learning, is further highlighted as a pathway for predictive alloy design. Beyond structural applications, Mg alloys demonstrate strong potential in cardiovascular stents, surgical devices, and biodegradable energy systems, enabling multifunctional and transient biomedical platforms.

papers.title: On the role of nanoparticle dispersion into melt pool dynamics and microstructure evolution during powder-bed fusion additive manufacturing
papers.abstract: Nanoparticle addition in metal additive manufacturing (AM) has been investigated as a method to strengthen mechanical properties by modulating microstructures. Although the effectiveness of nanoparticle addition is well recognised, the dynamic process of spatial dispersion is not satisfactorily understood since in-situ observation is difficult. High-fidelity numerical simulation by computational fluid dynamics (CFD) is utilised to understand the dispersion mechanisms induced by molten flow dynamics. The nanoparticle dynamics is strongly characterised by vortical flow motion. Differences in the physical properties among the three alloys (SS316L, IN718 and Ti-6Al-4V), especially the thermal diffusivity and kinematic viscosity, make the degree of dispersion different, and the hatch distance is also a factor for local degree of dispersion, which gives insights for seeking optimal process conditions. Coupled with the CFD results, grain growth simulation by the cellular automata (CA) method shows that nanoparticles can serve as initial nucleation sites and induce local columnar to equiaxed transition. The degree of finer grain evolution is dependent on local clustering of nanoparticles induced by the flow motion. The present study has paved the way for estimating and controlling microstructures for multiple additively manufactured alloys and will be extended to more detailed mechanical properties analysis in the future.

papers.abstract: Microwave medical systems for breast imaging and hyperthermia require iterative estimation of electric field distributions within heterogeneous tissues. Breast anatomy exhibits substantial geometric and compositional heterogeneity, with considerable variations in shape, tissue distribution, and dielectric properties across different cases. Accurate field estimation therefore requires high-resolution full-wave electromagnetic simulations, which are computationally demanding for time-sensitive clinical workflows. This study proposes a deep learning (DL)-based surrogate modeling approach for rapid prediction of electric field distributions in heterogeneous breast tissues under a fixed antenna configuration. The dataset consists of high-resolution dielectric property maps derived from Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI)-based breast models at 2.4 GHz. An anatomically consistent augmentation strategy was applied to increase data variability while preserving realistic tissue distributions, expanding the dataset to 4,878 breast slices. Corresponding electric field distributions were generated using a finite element method (FEM)-based solver as ground-truth labels for training and evaluating ResNet and U-Net architectures. A masked loss function was also employed to focus learning on heterogeneous breast tissue regions. Performance was evaluated on 504 test samples. ResNet achieved an average Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) of 10.01 ± 2.84 dB and a Normalized Mean Squared Error (NMSE) of 0.130 ± 0.113, whereas U-Net achieved 10.83 ± 2.68 dB and 0.105 ± 0.087, respectively. The masked-loss strategy further increased the average U-Net SNR by 0.12 dB. The results demonstrate that DL-based surrogate models can accurately reconstruct electric field distributions while avoiding repeated full-wave simulations, supporting rapid field prediction for microwave imaging and hyperthermia treatment-planning workflows.

papers.title: Dynamic Control Barrier Function-Based Model Predictive Control for Safety-Critical Systems
papers.abstract: This article proposes a safety-critical control framework for autonomous vehicles operating in dynamic environments. Dynamic obstacles are represented by online-updated oriented minimum bounding ellipses (MBEs), providing a compact and geometry-aware approximation of irregular obstacle shapes. Abarrier function is constructed from the minimum Euclidean distance between the vehicle and each fit ellipse, while the effect of the estimated obstacle motion is explicitly retained in the barrier derivative. The resulting dynamic control barrier function (DCBF) is incorporated into model predictive control (MPC) through discrete-time control barrier function (CBF) constraints. To balance safety conservatism and optimization feasibility under varying vehicle-obstacle interactions, a bounded sigmoid-based mechanism adjusts the CBF decay rate online. In addition, a constant-velocity Kalman filter (CV-KF) estimates obstacle positions and velocities from noisy measurements and propagates the estimated states over the MPC prediction horizon. The simulation and experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves safe and efficient obstacle avoidance in the tested dynamic scenarios.

papers.title: Evidence-Based Program Management Infrastructure for Joint Communication, Sensing, and Intelligence (JCSI) Systems in Sovereign Low-Altitude Unmanned Traffic Management
papers.abstract: This research establishes a mathematically rigorous, evidence-based program management framework addressing the critical operational "Bit-Transport Deconfliction Disconnect" inherent in low-altitude Unmanned Traffic Management (UTM) operations below 400 feet AGL. Under the directorial leadership and supervision of Anyanwu Obioma Anselam, a collaborative research initiative between AUAVL/NASRDA and FUTO treats UTM as an integrated Joint Communication, Sensing, and Intelligence (JCSI) optimization problem. The framework couples multi-agent stochastic trajectory optimization loops directly with physical network propagation profiles from the NigComSat-1R geostationary satellite infrastructure positioned at its strategic 42.5°E orbital slot. This integrated architecture serves as an innovative engineering and technology policy blueprint for indigenous, sovereign African space-terrestrial infrastructure integration, avoiding external dependency. To fulfill institutional Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and guarantee reproducibility for multi-agency stakeholders, three comparative computational modeling frameworks are rigorously benchmarked and analyzed: Response Surface Methodology (RSM), Artificial Neural Networks (ANN), and Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference Systems (ANFIS). Simulation metrics establish that while intelligent neuro-fuzzy architectures offer sub-millisecond execution speeds under epistemic wind shear field dynamics, parametric RSM formulations yield the explicit, auditable Pareto-optimal surfaces necessary for programmatic compliance verification and safety audits.

papers.title: Research trends and future agendas of feedback‐seeking behaviour in L2 learning: A systematic review
papers.abstract: Feedback‐seeking behaviour is an active learning strategy that has been reviewed in fields such as management and medical education. However, the existing literature lacks a comprehensive and domain‐specific review of learners' active efforts to obtain feedback in L2 (second/foreign language) learning. We systematically reviewed 62 eligible empirical studies of feedback‐seeking behaviour in L2 learning. Through qualitative coding, we examined the studies' theoretical and conceptual frameworks, research contexts, methodologies and major findings about the antecedents and outcomes of feedback‐seeking behaviour. First, prominent theoretical frameworks connected language learning mindsets and academic goals with feedback seeking; expectancy‐value and language socialization perspectives also informed this topic. Second, most studies focused on Chinese students in higher education and investigated their feedback‐seeking behaviour in English writing, while other languages and skills received less attention. Online and AI‐mediated writing studies were present but less common than classroom and non‐AI‐mediated writing studies. Third, the methodological review indicated that most studies relied on questionnaires (73%), while interviews were used in half of the included studies and structural equation modelling in 27%. Fourth, our qualitative synthesis found that antecedents of feedback‐seeking behaviour in L2 learning encompassed individual factors (e.g. motivational appraisals, cognition, learner attributes, dispositions and perceived costs) and external factors (feedback sources, social support and task/assessment features); reported outcomes included revision quality, learning process optimization, social relationships and academic‐writing socialization. Evidence of learning gains varied by feedback‐seeking strategy and learner proficiency. These findings suggest an ecological interpretation of interactions among learners, feedback sources, tasks and settings, while the predominance of self‐report and cross‐sectional designs limits causal claims. The review identifies priorities for longitudinal and observational research across a wider range of L2 learning contexts, with implications for learner‐centred feedback design. Context and implications Rationale for this study: Existing L2 feedback reviews have rarely synthesized learners' active efforts to obtain feedback across settings and tasks. Why the new findings matter: Across 62 included studies, feedback seeking reflected both learner motivation and available support. Links with learning varied by strategy and proficiency. Implications for language teachers, curriculum designers and researchers: Teachers and curriculum designers can clarify assessment criteria, share exemplars, offer peer feedback opportunities and allow time for questions and revision. They can help L2 learners evaluate and use feedback from teachers, peers and, where appropriate, AI tools. Researchers should trace requests, responses, revisions and learning across repeated feedback cycles and study more languages, skills and educational stages. These are promising approaches, but the current evidence is concentrated in university English writing, and many studies use self‐report or cross‐sectional designs. Further research should be encouraged.

papers.title: Explainable ensemble learning for chloride penetration (RCPT) and carbonation of concrete: comparative cross-mechanism interpretation with uncertainty quantification
papers.abstract: Chloride ingress and carbonation drive reinforcement corrosion but are usually predicted separately. Explainable ensemble machine learning models were developed for the rapid chloride penetration test (RCPT) charge passed and carbonation depth under a common protocol to compare their governing factors. Literature databases were screened to 145 RCPT records (20 sources) and 2012 carbonation records (45 sources). Five ensembles, including extra trees (ET) and extreme gradient boosting (XGB), were tuned by Bayesian optimization and benchmarked against linear, kernel and power-law models using hold-out testing, repeated 10 × 5-fold cross-validation (CV) and studywise validation. Conformal prediction intervals quantified uncertainty, and Shapley additive explanations and partial dependence interpreted model behavior. XGB predicted carbonation best (R2 = 0.815; RMSE = 3.64 mm; CV R2 = 0.797 ± 0.028), significantly outperforming all others. For RCPT, ET had the highest hold-out accuracy (R2 = 0.791; RMSE = 677.6 C), while ensembles performed comparably in CV. 95% intervals covered 96.6% (RCPT) and 96.3% (carbonation) of test observations. Water-to-binder ratio and binder-related inputs influenced both indicators; exposure conditions dominated carbonation, and ablation showed binder type governs RCPT. Studywise validation limited their use to the represented sources. A durability index combining both predictions outlined data needs for mix design.

papers.title: Advanced fault detection and diagnosis for induction motors using Chien-Physics-Informed Neural Networks and optimization techniques
papers.abstract: Model-based methods need to accurately model the sy-stem, which can be difficult with the nonlinear nature of motors. Insulation faults in induction motors (IMs) may result in significant production losses and disruption in an industrial application, so they are important. The aim of this research is to introduce a Fault Detection and Diagnosis (FDD) method based on the Chien-Physics-Informed Neural Networks (C-PINN) approach. The input signals of the Data Challenge 2021 data are pre-processed with Derivative-free Extended Kalman Filtering (DF-EKF) to eliminate noise and normalise the data. The High-Order Synchro-Extracting Transform (HOSET) is used to extract statistical features for improving diagnostics. The model is also enhanced by the Fractional Pelican African Vulture Optimisation (FPAVO) algorithm to overcome the problem of parameter optimisation in the C-PINN. The simulation results in MATLAB show that the proposed method was found to be more accurate (99.3%) and attained a higher true positive rate (0.993) and a lower false positive rate (0.007) than existing methods, and also reduced the computational complexity. Overall, this comprehensive system provides a more reliable and efficient way to detect faults, further improving the safety and durability of induction motors in industrial applications.

papers.title: Factors Influencing Learning Outcomes in Online Education Environments
papers.abstract: This study investigates the factors influencing online education outcomes, focusing on learner engagement, self-directed learning, active learning methods, the flipped classroom approach, flexibility, and accessibility. Using a quantitative research design, the study examined the extent to which these factors contribute to successful online learning outcomes. Data were collected through an online survey administered to students enrolled in online universities. SPSS version 23 was used to run data analysis. Of the 900 questionnaires distributed, 849 valid responses were received, resulting in a response rate of 94.3%. Multiple regression analysis was employed to test the proposed hypotheses and assess the relationships between the independent variables and online education outcomes. The findings indicate that all five factors exert a positive and statistically significant influence on online education outcomes, supporting the proposed hypotheses. The regression model explained 59.2% of the variance in online education outcomes (R 2 = 0.592), demonstrating strong explanatory power. Learner engagement (β = 0.301) and self-directed learning (β = 0.297) emerged as the most influential predictors, highlighting the importance of active participation and autonomous learning behaviors. Active learning methods (β = 0.279) also significantly enhanced learning effectiveness, while the flipped classroom approach, flexibility, and accessibility showed positive and significant contributions. The results emphasize the need for learner-centered, interactive, flexible, and accessible online learning environments. These findings provide valuable implications for educators, institutions, and policymakers seeking to improve the quality and effectiveness of online education.

papers.title: Mechanical integrity-preserving topographical engineering establishes a geometrically instructive zirconia implant interface that promotes osteogenic responses.
papers.abstract: Next-generation implants are expected to move beyond passive bone acceptance and provide defined interfacial cues capable of guiding cellular responses. Here, we propose a topographical engineering strategy for zirconia dental implants to balance osteogenic performance with mechanical integrity. Using nanoparticle jetting, microporous and microgrooved architectures were directly written into the zirconia surface, enabling one-step integration of topographical patterning and structural fabrication without sandblasting, acid etching, or other post-treatments. Gaussian process regression was used to identify high-performing microstructural candidates, followed by multiscale surface characterization, cellular functional assays, and mechanistic validation. The encoded topographies promoted cell proliferation, spreading, and osteogenic differentiation, accompanied by cytoskeletal remodeling, ROCK-dependent YAP activation, and increased expression of osteogenic markers, including RUNX2. We further translated this strategy into a region-adaptive zirconia implant (RAZI), in which distinct topographies were spatially encoded to meet site-specific mechanical and osteogenic demands. This design preserved high manufacturing fidelity and favorable mechanical performance while coupling macroscale mechanical adaptation with microscale topographical cues associated with osteogenic responses. In a beagle mandibular implantation model, RAZI exhibited favorable osseointegration at 12 weeks, with bone-to-implant contact (BIC) and bone area (BA) reaching 74.55 ± 4.67% and 75.68 ± 6.67%, respectively. These findings provide a region-adaptive topographical engineering framework for next-generation metal-free dental implants.

papers.abstract: This study aims to formulate teaching principles, strategies, implementation stages, and assessment methods that support changes in students' learning behavior and daily life behavior. The analytical framework is based on Elaine B. Johnson's contextual teaching and learning approach, which connects learning materials with real-life experiences, independence, collaboration, and authentic assessment, as well as Jody Capehart's ideas on understanding students, caring, role modeling, communication, and discipline in Christian education. This study employs a qualitative method with a literature review approach, examining the two primary books, Indonesian-language books, and relevant national journal articles. Data were collected through documentation studies and analyzed using thematic content analysis, involving information selection, coding, theme categorization, source comparison, and synthesis. The findings formulate six teaching steps: identifying students' needs, establishing behavioral change objectives, selecting relevant learning experiences, engaging students through teacher role modeling, guiding reflection, and supporting the application and development of positive habits. The proposed strategies integrate contextual and active learning, differentiated learning support, constructive communication, and educative discipline. Changes in learning behavior and daily life behavior are recommended to be assessed through repeated observations, portfolios, reflections, self-assessments, and developmental records. This framework requires support from schools and families, as well as further implementation to examine its suitability within student learning contexts. Keywords: Teaching Strategies, Behavioral Change, Contextual Learning.

summary_en.motivation: The study seeks to articulate teaching principles and strategies that foster changes in students' learning and everyday behavior.
summary_en.method: A qualitative literature review applies thematic content analysis to two primary books and related Indonesian journal articles.
summary_en.result: Six instructional steps and several assessment approaches are proposed to support behavioral change.
summary_en.validation: Validation relies solely on documentary analysis without empirical or quantitative testing.
